acceptance_criteria: A paper goal stores figure_slots as structured FigureSpec objects (x/y/plot_kind/comparison + target_question_id/target_claim_id + origin EntityRef), validated with extra='forbid'. Legacy list[str] figure_slots still validate and round-trip (coerced to FigureSpec(slot=s)). A FigureSpec can be created with an origin note/session BEFORE any Visualization or Analysis exists. Invalid/unknown fields are rejected. Tests in tests/test_goals.py cover: structured create, legacy-string coercion, invalid-field rejection, and origin EntityRef round-trip. No new table or migration; change confined to the attributes blob. Stays within the build-vs-buy boundary (documented).
description: Goals can be specified before their data/analysis exist — a PI sketches 'plot firing rate vs contrast as Figure 3' on a whiteboard during a lab meeting, months before the recording session or analysis. Today a paper goal's planned figures are bare strings (PaperAttributes.figure_slots: list[str] in goals_attributes.py) and a CANDIDATE_FIGURE GoalLink can only target an already-rendered Visualization entity (which requires analysis_id + file_path). So two things go unrecorded: (1) the INTENT of a planned figure — what is meant to be plotted, against what, to answer which question/claim; and (2) the MECHANISM of its specification — which note/session/whiteboard-asset it originated from, when, and via what medium. This promotes the planned-figure slot from a string to a structured, machine-readable FigureSpec carrying intent + origin provenance, WITHOUT inventing a new entity or table. Follow-on to lab-tracker-co0 (closed).
design: Add a FigureSpec Pydantic model in goals_attributes.py (extra='forbid') and change PaperAttributes.figure_slots from list[str] to list[FigureSpec]. FigureSpec fields: slot (str, required label e.g. 'Figure 3'); intent — x (str|None), y (str|None), grouping (str|None), plot_kind (str|None e.g. scatter/line/bar), comparison (str|None free-text 'this against that'); semantic edges — target_question_id (UUID|None), target_claim_id (UUID|None); origin provenance — origin (EntityRef|None pointing at the note/session/whiteboard-asset), specified_at (date|None), medium (str|None e.g. 'whiteboard','lab_meeting'). Lives in the validated attributes JSON blob — NO schema migration, NO new table. Realization path stays complementary, not duplicated: when a real Visualization is later created, a CANDIDATE_FIGURE GoalLink with slot == FigureSpec.slot links it and candidate->committed marks the slot filled; FigureSpec describes the PLAN, GoalLink records FULFILLMENT. Backward compat: accept legacy list[str] on read and coerce each string s to FigureSpec(slot=s); stored-JSON migration is lazy (on next write). Wire through goals_attributes validation, schemas.py goal create/update payloads, the MCP write tool (suggest_new_goal / update_goal already exist), and the IMAGE_ONLY graph-draft path so a whiteboard photo -> Note.raw_asset -> suggested goal can auto-populate FigureSpec.origin. Boundary: this is the LIGHTWEIGHT option chosen over a first-class PlannedVisualization entity precisely to avoid scope creep — it must stay a thin semantic-metadata layer and NOT become a slot-coverage board, figure-layout editor, or plotting tool (docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md).
notes: Existing hooks to reuse: GraphDraftMode.IMAGE_ONLY, GraphDraftSemanticType.SUGGEST_NEW_GOAL / LINK_NODE_TO_GOAL, Note.raw_asset (whiteboard photo), GoalRelation.CANDIDATE_FIGURE, GoalLink.slot, GoalLinkStatus.candidate/committed. Heavier alternative (deferred): a first-class PlannedVisualization entity that CANDIDATE_FIGURE can target before any Analysis exists and that is later realized into a Visualization — revisit only if repeated need proves it.
title: Planned-figure specs: promote goal figure_slot from string to structured FigureSpec with origin provenance

acceptance_criteria: Human-gate invariants enforced and covered by tests (C1-C3); in-process scheduler is opt-in, default-off, drafting-only, and structurally unable to commit or accept (C4); scheduled runs are visibly distinguished in the web app (C5); docs updated (C6); uv run pytest -q and ruff check . pass for touched areas.
description: Make the daily-review AI proposal generation run server-side on an opt-in in-process schedule, while making drafting-only (never autonomous commit) a structurally enforced invariant rather than a property of absent code. Context: the graph-draft pipeline already runs the LLM inside the FastAPI process (services/graph_draft_service.py run_due_graph_draft_batches calls make_graph_draft_client and draft_from_batch) and surfaces proposals at /app/batches; only the trigger clock is external (cron or Windows Scheduled Task per docs/scheduled-daily-review.md). Danger: the commit/accept gate trusts role==ADMIN (project_authorization.py require_owner at :175 short-circuits on has_global_admin at :40, which checks only actor.role==Role.ADMIN), which the scheduler actor already holds (run_due requires has_global_admin), and a ready-made non-human admin exists (middleware.py:90 local_auth_context). acceptance_mode AUTO_ACCEPTED is reserved (models.py:318) but never assigned and unguarded, and the commit path never inspects acceptance_mode, so an in-process scheduler is the exact edit that could silently arm autonomous commits while the whole test suite still passes. Wall before clock.
design: Build order: C1 and C2 in parallel, then C3, then C4, then C5 and C6. Out of scope: distributed locking and multi-instance leader election (single-machine deployment; claim_due compare-and-set suffices for one DB). Coordinate the C5 scheduled-run indicator with the broader review-UI rework in epic lab-tracker-udv1 (Morning Read). Honors retained-v1-surface.md:97-99 (no autonomous graph commits) and docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md.
title: Server-side daily-review drafting behind an enforced human-gate

acceptance_criteria: Stamping or persisting AUTO_ACCEPTED raises a clear error; unit tests cover the stamp path and the repo write path; existing HUMAN_SELECTED and BULK_ACCEPTED behavior unchanged; ruff and pytest green.
description: Keep the AcceptanceMode.AUTO_ACCEPTED enum value (models.py:318) for provenance honesty, but make it inert-by-guard so it can never be persisted until deliberately implemented. Raise if AUTO_ACCEPTED is passed to _stamp_operation_acceptance (services/graph_draft_service.py:865) or update_graph_change_operation (services/graph_draft_service.py:803), and reject it at the repository write path (sqlalchemy_repository_parts/graph_drafts.py:71). Today only HUMAN_SELECTED and BULK_ACCEPTED are ever assigned and AUTO_ACCEPTED has zero assignment sites, so this guard changes no current behavior and only closes the latent path.
notes: Implemented: AUTO_ACCEPTED guard at top of _stamp_operation_acceptance (graph_draft_service.py) raises ValidationError; defense-in-depth guard in operation_to_model (sqlalchemy_repository_parts/graph_drafts.py) rejects persisting AUTO_ACCEPTED. Enum value kept for provenance honesty. Tests appended to tests/test_graph_drafts.py (autonomy guardrails section). Pending full-suite confirmation.
title: Forbid AUTO_ACCEPTED from being stamped or committed (tripwire)

acceptance_criteria: A non-interactive automation admin actor is rejected by commit_graph_change_set, bulk_accept, and per-op accept; an interactive human owner or admin still passes; run_due drafting still works for the automation actor; tests cover both principal kinds; ruff and pytest green.
description: Today the human gate on commit is enforced only at the HTTP route layer (bearer token); the service trusts role==ADMIN. require_owner (services/project_authorization.py:175) short-circuits on has_global_admin (:40, which checks only actor.role==Role.ADMIN). Make commit_graph_change_set (services/graph_draft_service.py:1187), bulk_accept_graph_change_operations (:890), and per-operation accept via update_graph_change_operation (:803) require an interactive human PrincipalType, not merely an admin role. Introduce a non-interactive automation/system PrincipalType (AuthContext already carries principal_type) so an automation actor with admin role can DRAFT via run_due but cannot ACCEPT or COMMIT. This is the structural wall that makes the in-process scheduler safe.
notes: Design refinement vs original framing: the gate is a fail-closed ALLOW-LIST, not require-USER. New PrincipalType.SYSTEM (auth.py). AuthContext.is_interactive = principal in {USER, DEVICE, SERVICE}, so the lpat SERVICE consumer-client/MCP commit path is preserved; only SYSTEM automation is blocked. ProjectAuthorizationPolicy.require_interactive raises AuthError; called in commit_graph_change_set (after require_owner) and in _stamp_operation_acceptance ACCEPTED branch (covers per-op accept AND bulk_accept). system_auth_context() factory added in app_parts/middleware.py for the C4 scheduler. Tests appended to tests/test_graph_drafts.py. Pending full-suite confirmation.
title: Enforce interactive-human principal at the service-layer commit and accept gates

acceptance_criteria: Tests (a) through (d) implemented and green; each fails if its guard is removed (verify by temporary mutation); no production code change required beyond C1 and C2.
description: Pin the cross-cutting invariants that catch the regression class the auto_accept audit flagged, so a future scheduler edit cannot silently bypass them. Assert: (a) a non-interactive system actor cannot commit a READY change set; (b) no committed operation may carry acceptance_mode==auto_accepted; (c) a change set whose operations are all PROPOSED is rejected by commit in isolation (services/graph_draft_service.py:1211); (d) the scheduled drafting path leaves change_set status=READY with operations PROPOSED and never calls _stamp_operation_acceptance or commit. Tests live under tests/ and run in the existing CI pytest gate.
title: Autonomy-invariant regression tests

acceptance_criteria: With the flag off, behavior is unchanged (default). With it on, due batches draft on the interval without an external scheduler; the loop survives a tick exception; a heartbeat is recorded; the scheduler actor cannot commit or accept (C3 invariants hold); ruff and pytest green.
description: Add an opt-in, default-off in-process scheduler so the daily-review trigger clock runs inside the FastAPI process instead of an external cron or Scheduled Task. In app_parts/runtime.py make_lifespan, when a new setting LAB_TRACKER_DAILY_REVIEW_IN_PROCESS_SCHEDULER (default false, plus a poll-seconds setting) is enabled, start an asyncio interval task that periodically calls run_due_graph_draft_batches with the non-interactive system actor from C2, and cancel/await it cleanly on shutdown. Requirements: offload the blocking provider call off the event loop (anyio.to_thread or run_in_threadpool); wrap each tick in try/except with structured logging so an exception cannot kill the loop; emit a heartbeat (usage event or batch-run record) so a silently dead loop is visible; document single-worker-only. Keep POST /batches/run-due and /batches/run-now and the external trigger scripts working as-is; the in-process timer is an additional reversible trigger. Because the system actor cannot commit (C2), this triggers drafting only.
title: Opt-in in-process daily-review scheduler

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled runs and drafts show a clear scheduled indicator distinct from manual ones in the batches surface; created_by for scheduled change sets reads as a labeled system principal not a real user; npm run test:frontend, npm run lint:frontend, and npm run build pass.
description: Make a scheduler-generated draft visibly distinct from a human-initiated one at /app/batches. GraphDraftBatchRun.trigger already records SCHEDULED vs MANUAL; surface it (and the non-interactive system actor as the run origin) in the batch list, run history, and PendingBatchBanner (frontend_src/features/batches.jsx) so reviewers can tell a draft was produced unattended. Minimal indicator only; coordinate with the broader review-UI rework in epic lab-tracker-udv1 (Morning Read). Frontend bundle changes require npm build and the frontend gates per CLAUDE.md.
title: Surface scheduled-run indicator in the web app

acceptance_criteria: docs/scheduled-daily-review.md updated with the in-process option, the drafting-only guarantee, the single-worker note, and single-trigger guidance; doc-drift guards (epic lab-tracker-bi0c) still pass.
description: Update docs/scheduled-daily-review.md to present the in-process scheduler (C4) as an opt-in convenience layer alongside the existing external trigger (cron, Windows Scheduled Task, or Claude routine), not a replacement. Document how to enable the flag, that it triggers drafting only and never commits, the single-worker constraint, and pick-exactly-one-trigger guidance to avoid running both. Note that the external scripts remain the documented fallback and survive app restarts.
title: Operational docs for the in-process scheduler

acceptance_criteria: Children land or are explicitly deferred/wont-do with rationale; graph-draft behavior remains unchanged; MCP read/write classification is guarded; assistant consultation policy has a canonical source; quality gates pass for touched areas.
description: Behavior-preserving internal-cohesion refactor for Lab Tracker's assistant-facing boundary, grounded in the actual codebase and the retained-v1 product surface. The goal is to make graph drafting, MCP tool classification, and assistant policy easier to inspect and maintain without changing domain behavior.

Avoid a capability descriptor engine until there is a runtime consumer. Do not duplicate existing functional beads such as n5kp.8, n5kp.9, n5kp.4, or 99x.4. Human-gated graph changes and API-backed writes remain the boundary.

acceptance_criteria: Leaf modules exist for errors, schema/constants, and prompts; existing imports from lab_tracker.graph_drafting continue to work; generated prompt/schema output is unchanged; backend tests and ruff pass for touched code.
description: graph_drafting.py is a large mixed-concern module containing GraphDraftingError, graph patch schema/constants, three provider clients, the provider factory, prompt builders, and response parsing. Extract the dependency-free leaves first: errors, schema/constants, and prompt builders. Preserve lab_tracker.graph_drafting as the import-stable compatibility shim.

title: Extract graph_drafting.py leaf modules behind re-export shim

acceptance_criteria: list_question_refactors is exposed/classified read-only with a focused, future-resilient registry guard test; describe_schema reports accurate natural_key for project/question/note (or quickstart warns creates are non-idempotent) so the agent schema no longer claims natural_key=[] where the client dedups on a real key; no MCP write behavior changes; n5kp.8/n5kp.9 remain separate work; uv run pytest -q and uv run ruff check . pass.
description:
Two verified ways the agent-facing MCP write surface misdescribes itself; both are metadata-honesty fixes with NO write-behavior change.

(1) Classification mis-file: lab_tracker_list_question_refactors is a read-style list tool but is registered among mutating tools (mcp_tools/write.py:451). Reclassify it and add a property-oriented guard test for the read/write registries.

(2) Idempotency honesty: schema_metadata.py sets natural_key=[] for EVERY entity (lines ~112-180), so lab_tracker_describe_schema tells agents no natural key exists -- while the consumer client (lab_tracker_client/client.py) dedups on real natural keys (find_project_by_name, find_question_by_text, find_note_by_marker) and the raw MCP create path is non-idempotent (question_service.create_question mints uuid4 + unconditional save, question_service.py:104,140). An agent re-issuing a create after an ambiguous tool result silently duplicates a node in the system-of-record graph, and the schema misleads it about how to avoid that.

This is the only salvage from the dropped capability-descriptor system; per-tool provenance-effect/evidence-safety flags and an error-code taxonomy stay dropped (no runtime consumer). Folded here, not a new bead, because it is the same "describe the write surface honestly" theme.
design: (1) Move/register list_question_refactors through the read surface; guard test asserts registry properties and that a read tool cannot sit in the write registry, WITHOUT freezing the full tool list. (2) Populate the existing natural_key field in schema_metadata.py for project/question/note to match the consumer-client upsert convention (project=[name], question=[project_id,text], note=[project_id,first_line_marker]) and/or add one lab_tracker_quickstart sentence (mcp_tools/resources.py) warning MCP create_* tools are non-idempotent -- list before re-creating. Do NOT add provenance-effect/evidence-safety/error-code descriptors. Coordinate with n5kp.8/n5kp.9 (same write surface, functional bugs, not subsumed).
notes: Scope addition (2026-06-16, deep-dive-dropped-scope workflow): natural_key honesty fix is the sole verified, in-scope salvage from the dropped D descriptor bead; scope-hawk + product-safety judges both recommended folding it here. Items 2/4/5 stay dropped; item 3 (duplicate-write DB unique constraint) is a separate potential P3 data-integrity bead, out of this epic.
title: Honest MCP write-surface metadata: read/write mis-file + natural-key disclosure

acceptance_criteria: There is one canonical source for assistant task kinds, consultation policy, and decision-context failure vocabulary; current MCP resources/generated activation text consume that source; existing decision-context behavior and tests remain unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: Child beads exist for the dual runtime, service composition, graph draft split, MCP split, mapper decision, status transition cleanup, Pydantic validation migration, authorization policy, app factory split, and small review nits. Dependencies show the hard sequencing constraints. No code or research-record changes are required by this epic itself.
description:
Own the architecture cleanup roadmap from the code-quality review. The review identified two high-leverage structural problems, the LabTrackerAPI mixin facade and the dual in-memory/repository runtime, plus several medium-sized module and validation cleanup tracks.

This epic is issue-tracker work only. It should coordinate incremental refactors while preserving the retained-v1 runtime surface and avoiding changes to Lab Tracker research records.
design: Map review P0 items to bead priority 1; reserve bead priority 0 for broken builds, security, or data loss. Keep product feature beads independent unless implementation later proves a direct dependency. Child beads should be small enough to land as separate PRs with tests.
title: Epic: Architecture cleanup from code-quality review

acceptance_criteria: No parallel dict store remains in runtime code. Reads and writes go through LabTrackerRepository-backed persistence. Existing API behavior is unchanged for retained-v1 workflows. Tests that previously depended on InMemoryStore use repository-backed fixtures. Backend tests pass.
description: Remove the parallel InMemoryStore path and make LabTrackerAPI/service reads and writes use the repository path unconditionally. The current dual runtime keeps a dict-backed store and SQLAlchemy repository active in the same process, forcing every read/write through cache/repository branching and whole-store hydration after failed writes.
design: Delete InMemoryStore, hydrate_from_repository, _uses_in_memory_entity_cache, _get_cached_entity, and repository/store branching from API and services. Tests that need fast feedback should use repository-backed SQLite fixtures rather than the parallel dict store. Preserve the retained-v1 public behavior and API method names while simplifying persistence internally.
title: Retire dual in-memory/repository runtime

acceptance_criteria: Small nits are resolved in a focused sweep with tests where behavior changes. SQLAlchemy repository compatibility-barrel policy is explicit. Root database artifact policy is clarified, with fixtures moved under tests/fixtures only if they are intentionally committed test data. Any larger response-typing, lint-rule, or structural work is split into follow-up beads instead of hidden inside this sweep.
description: Batch the smaller code-quality review findings that do not need their own large refactor. This includes cross-module private helper names, deferred-action failure comments, Ruff configuration, SQLAlchemy compatibility-barrel policy, and database artifact hygiene.
design: Keep this bead small and safe. Publicize or relocate underscore-prefixed helpers that are imported across modules, explain intentionally swallowed deferred-action failures, clarify whether sqlalchemy_repository.py remains an import-stable compatibility barrel or should receive a dated removal TODO, and document DB artifact policy. Root .db and .db.backup files are currently ignored and untracked, so clarify hygiene/fixture placement rather than implying tracked cleanup. Ruff rule expansion belongs in the separate Ruff bead; this bead may only coordinate or reference it. Create follow-up beads rather than expanding scope for large response typing or module redesign work.
title: Sweep small architecture review nits

acceptance_criteria: finish_request(committed=...) is removed or reduced to a non-public compatibility shim that no caller must use. Middleware no longer tracks a mutable committed flag to decide deferred hooks. after_commit hooks run only after a successful commit; after_rollback hooks run on rollback/error paths. Route/session tests cover successful commit and rollback/error behavior. Backend tests pass.
description: Replace finish_request(committed=...) and middleware-level mutable commit flags with a context-managed request lifecycle. The current caller must remember whether a database session committed before deferred after-commit or after-rollback hooks run, which is easy to misuse on exception or rollback paths.
design: Introduce a request-scope/context-manager API that owns repository binding, commit/rollback outcome, deferred-action dispatch, and cleanup. The FastAPI database middleware should enter the request scope, run the handler, commit or roll back through one explicit lifecycle path, and let the scope fire after_commit only after a successful commit and after_rollback only on rollback/error. Keep public route and LabTrackerAPI behavior unchanged.
title: Make request lifecycle context-managed

acceptance_criteria: Representative decision-context outputs remain stable for retained-v1 use cases. Querying, selection, compacting/building, and orchestration responsibilities are separated into focused modules or classes. Focused unit tests cover the extracted parts and existing decision-context/MCP tests pass.
description: Decompose decision_context.py into focused modules. The current decision-context assembly is large enough to obscure separate responsibilities such as querying graph data, selecting relevant records, compacting payloads, and shaping the MCP decision-context response.
design: Split the implementation into focused builders/query/use-case modules while preserving lab_tracker_get_decision_context behavior. Keep the MCP/API-facing response shape stable, and extract pure or easily unit-tested pieces first so representative context packets can be regression-tested.
title: Split decision context assembly into focused modules

acceptance_criteria: pyproject.toml selects E, F, I, B, UP, and SIM or an equivalent explicit Ruff rule set. Ruff findings from the expanded rules are fixed or narrowly ignored with rationale. uv run ruff check . passes. Larger refactors discovered during lint cleanup are tracked as follow-up beads rather than hidden in this chore.
description: Expand the Ruff lint configuration beyond E/F to include inexpensive correctness and modernization checks. The review specifically called out isort, bugbear, pyupgrade, and simplify rules as cheap wins.
design: Add I, B, UP, and SIM to the Ruff lint selection, run Ruff, fix resulting findings, and document any intentional ignores narrowly. Keep behavioral changes minimal; split any nontrivial cleanup discovered by the lint expansion into separate beads.
title: Expand Ruff lint rule set and fix findings

acceptance_criteria: Service dependencies are explicit in constructors instead of hidden through mixin inheritance. LabTrackerAPI continues to expose the current flat method names and existing route/MCP behavior remains unchanged. Request-scoped and singleton/root construction paths are represented by distinct types or otherwise made explicit. Representative services can be unit-tested without instantiating the full facade. New service write paths use an explicit unit-of-work/context-manager pattern rather than lambda-passed repository operations. Backend tests pass.
description: Replace the LabTrackerAPI inheritance facade with explicit service objects while preserving the current flat LabTrackerAPI public method surface. The current class inherits many service mixins that implicitly share repository, raw storage, and request context through self, which hides dependencies and makes service-level unit testing difficult.
design: Introduce a ServiceContext that carries the active repository/unit-of-work, raw storage, request context, and any shared service helpers. Convert *ServiceMixin classes into normal service classes that receive this context and any explicit service dependencies via constructors. LabTrackerAPI remains a thin compatibility facade exposing the existing flat methods used by routes, MCP paths, and tests; it delegates internally to composed services. Split singleton/root API construction from request-scoped API construction where practical so repository/request-context availability is enforced by types or constructors instead of runtime optional checks. Replace lambda-passing repository writes with an explicit unit-of-work/context-manager style in the new services rather than carrying _run_repository_write(lambda repository: ...) forward.
title: Replace LabTrackerAPI service mixins with composed services

acceptance_criteria: Graph draft behavior is unchanged for retained-v1 note-scoped review. Builder, validator, and applier responsibilities are separated and covered with focused unit tests. Existing graph draft integration tests pass.
description: Break up the large graph draft service module into focused, testable components. The current service mixes workflow orchestration, context-packet construction, model patch validation, patch application, and permission checks in one large module.
design: Extract GraphContextBuilder, GraphPatchValidator, GraphPatchApplier, and a smaller GraphDraftService orchestrator. Prefer pure functions/classes for context building and validation. Avoid broad constructor rewiring until the service-composition direction is stable; low-risk pure extraction can start earlier.
title: Split graph draft service into context builder, validator, applier, and orchestrator

acceptance_criteria: python -m lab_tracker.mcp_server still starts the MCP server. Existing MCP tests pass. Tool payload and response behavior is unchanged. No direct DB writes are introduced.
description: Split the large MCP server module into the API HTTP client, grouped MCP tool modules, and a small registration/entrypoint layer. The current file combines auth retry client behavior, many MCP tool definitions, schema helpers, and module startup.
design: Create a client module for HTTP/auth/retry behavior, grouped tool modules by aggregate or workflow, and a server/entrypoint module that registers tools. Preserve the API-backed boundary: MCP tools call the Lab Tracker API and do not write directly to the database.
title: Split MCP server into client, tool modules, and registration entrypoint

acceptance_criteria: The bead records a concrete written direction for domain models, ORM models, Pydantic schemas, and mapper responsibilities, including why the chosen tradeoff is worth it for retained-v1. One pilot entity demonstrates the chosen approach without regressing persistence or API behavior. Follow-up implementation beads are created for wider migration or cleanup if needed. Backend tests relevant to the pilot pass.
description: Make an explicit design decision for whether Lab Tracker should keep paying the cost of separate domain models, SQLAlchemy ORM models, Pydantic schemas, and hand-written mappers. The current architecture is clean, but the three-representation model creates a large maintenance multiplier and the mapper layer must be updated manually for each field.
design: Evaluate the full representation strategy, not just mapper boilerplate: keep separate domain/ORM/schema layers, collapse domain and ORM with SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed models plus Pydantic from_attributes, adopt SQLModel, derive schemas from domain/ORM models, or generate mapper boilerplate. Record the chosen path and rationale in the bead before broad implementation. Use one pilot entity to prove persistence behavior, validation/wire behavior, migration cost, and test strategy before spawning broader implementation beads.
notes:
2026-05-28 representation decision for retained-v1:

Keep the three explicit representations for now. Domain models remain the service/repository contract and the place where retained-v1 domain fields are expressed without SQLAlchemy session behavior leaking upward. SQLAlchemy ORM models remain persistence-only database rows. Pydantic schemas remain the HTTP/MCP wire/input boundary rather than being generated from ORM models during retained-v1.

Do not collapse to SQLAlchemy-as-domain, SQLModel, or generated schemas in this phase. Those options could delete code, but they would also couple route payload shape, persistence mapping, and migration details during an active architecture cleanup. The safer tradeoff is to keep the boundary and reduce its maintenance cost.

Mapper responsibility stays explicit but should move from one monolithic sqlalchemy_mappers.py file into focused aggregate/entity modules with narrow tests and a compatibility barrel for existing imports. The pilot entity is Project: extract Project mapping into a focused mapper module, wire repository persistence through it, preserve the old import surface, and cover mapper plus project persistence/API behavior. Follow-up work should split the remaining mapper groups in the same style.
title: Decide whether the three-representation model layer is earning its keep

description: Why: scheduled graph drafting currently depends on an external cron on a client machine polling POST /batches/run-due (never installed on the workstation deployment — see lab-tracker-mt3n), scheduled batch drafts are authored by the scheduler's admin credential which collides with the author-only edit/submit gate on shared multi-user hosts, cadence/settings are per-project so reviews cannot be user-specific, and the single-shot structured-output draft call cannot look up existing graph nodes before proposing (duplicate-proposal risk). What: move the drafting heartbeat and the proposal-writing agent onto the server host, partition batch generation per (project, note author) with a designated reviewer, and replace the single-shot draft call with a tool-using agent behind the existing GraphDraftClient protocol. Design doc: docs/server-resident-agentic-drafting-design.md. Human gate is unchanged and strengthened: agents propose, only interactive humans accept/commit.
notes: Emerged from architecture discussion 2026-07-02. Dependency order: gate (.1, verified already landed on mainline 2026-07-02 and closed) -> job runner/ticker (.2) -> agentic draft client (.4); user-partitioned batches (.3) is independent of .2/.4.

acceptance_criteria: A SYSTEM- or SERVICE-principal call to accept/accept-all/commit raises an authorization error on every code path (service layer, not just routes); tests assert this for graph_draft_service accept, bulk accept, and commit; existing interactive flows unaffected.

Before autonomous agents run on the server host, this must be true by construction, fail-closed. What: port or reimplement the structural gate so that a non-interactive principal (SYSTEM, SERVICE) attempting accept-op, accept-all, or commit fails closed at the authorization layer regardless of call path, with tests covering the SYSTEM principal and service PATs.
notes:
Precondition for the agentic draft client and the in-process scheduler running as SYSTEM. See vision.md's note on the unmerged-branch gate; verify whether that branch still exists and is portable before reimplementing.
Verification 2026-07-02 (adversarial review pass on the design doc): the structural gate is ALREADY on mainline — commits 6889069 '(feat): enforce structural human-commit gate on graph drafts' and 57277e6 '(feat): exclude service tokens from the graph-draft review gate' (both 2026-07-02, prescribed by bead lab-tracker-09ok, which no longer resolves in bd). require_interactive (project_authorization.py:43-60) enforced at accept (graph_draft_service.py:901 via _stamp_operation_acceptance, covering single + bulk accept) and commit (:1228); auto_accepted rejected at service (:895-899) and repository (sqlalchemy_repository_parts/graph_drafts.py:56-58) layers; tests at tests/test_graph_drafts.py:2452/2462/2472 cover SYSTEM cannot commit/bulk-accept/accept plus service-token 401s. Acceptance criteria are met by existing mainline code. Stale vision.md status paragraph (240-245) amended in the design-doc PR.
title: Land the structural human-commit gate in mainline (fail-closed)

acceptance_criteria: With the flag on, due batches run without any external scheduler (multi-worker safe via existing CAS claims); draft generation executes in the worker, not in request handlers; run-now enqueues instead of blocking; run-due endpoint still works; vision.md and scheduled-daily-review.md amended; flag off preserves today's behavior exactly.
description: Why: the drafting heartbeat is currently an external cron/launchd/Task Scheduler job on a client machine curling admin-only POST /batches/run-due; its absence produces no error and it was never installed on the workstation deployment (lab-tracker-mt3n). The DB already does the real scheduling (per-project next_run_at, compare-and-set claim_due, deterministic batch_key), so the server can safely self-tick. Agentic drafting (sibling bead) also needs draft generation off the request thread: run-due currently does N projects x LLM calls synchronously inside one HTTP request. What: (1) a lifespan asyncio ticker behind a config flag that fires due batches as the SYSTEM principal; (2) a DB-backed job table (generalizing the GraphDraftBatchRun pattern: status, claims via compare-and-set, error_metadata) and an in-process worker that executes draft-generation jobs; (3) keep POST /batches/run-due for cloud schedulers; installer scripts become a documented fallback. Amend vision.md's 'zero background machinery' paragraph and scheduled-daily-review.md when this ships.
notes: Supersedes the operational need behind lab-tracker-mt3n once shipped (leave mt3n open until then). Ticker actor: SYSTEM principal via system_auth_context(), which currently has no production callers. Works for the desktop-launcher topology too (solo user gets drafts-waiting UX with zero installers).
title: In-process scheduler tick + DB-backed draft job queue and worker

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled batches produce one draft per (project, user-with-new-staged-notes) window; the assignee (an ordinary contributor) can edit/accept/submit their draft on an auth-enabled shared host; created_by on scheduled drafts is the triggering principal, review_assignee is the target user; per-(project,user) cadence rows migrate cleanly from existing per-project rows; note-scoped (non-batch) drafts keep author==creator semantics unchanged.
description: Why: draft review is user-specific — accepting, editing, and submitting are all gated on the change set author with only a global-admin override (graph_draft_service.py _is_graph_change_set_author ~:1287; submit ~:958; op edit/accept path via _ensure_graph_change_set_editable ~:1310) — but scheduled batch drafts are stamped created_by from the calling actor, i.e. the scheduler's admin credential (~:373 via run_due). On a shared multi-user host no ordinary contributor can work a scheduled draft; the solo-SQLite deployment masks this because every request is the same local-tester identity. Generation must be FOR a user. What: partition batch generation per (project, note author): the batch window covers only staged notes captured by that user; batch_key gains the user dimension; cadence settings become per (project, user) with a project-level default. Add a review_assignee field on GraphChangeSet and re-key ALL author-keyed review gates — accept/reject of operations, bulk-accept, edit, submit — from creator to assignee (concretely, _is_graph_change_set_author resolves to the assignee on scheduled drafts; re-keying only edit/submit would leave the assignee unable to accept). Attribution honesty: created_by remains the triggering principal (SYSTEM/scheduler) — do NOT stamp created_by with the assignee. Owner-only commit stays project-level. Cross-user synthesis in one window is intentionally given up; ops cite their source notes. Doc amendments when this ships: retained-v1-surface.md (per-project -> per-(project,user) batch settings) and review-and-commit-model.md (author-keyed review description).
notes: Related: lab-tracker-udv1.7 (per-user reminder time/timezone — the notification layer on top of this), lab-tracker-udv1.1 (committer role). There is currently no per-user settings storage at all (UserModel is username/hash/role only), so the settings scope change is new schema. Migration: check 'uv run alembic heads' prints exactly one before adding.
title: User-partitioned batch generation with designated reviewer (review_assignee)

acceptance_criteria: Agentic client is protocol-compatible and selectable via LAB_TRACKER_GRAPH_DRAFT_PROVIDER (or equivalent setting); drafts it produces flow through the unchanged human review lifecycle; the agent has no write path (read-only tools enforced structurally, not by prompt); provenance fields stamped; single-shot providers remain available as fallback; drafting via the agent never executes inside an HTTP request handler.
description: Why: today's proposal writer is a single-shot structured-output call (graph_drafting.py) that cannot look anything up, so it cannot search for existing questions/claims before proposing — the known duplicate-node-proposal risk (list-before-create). A tool-using agent that reads graph context, searches existing nodes, then emits the same structured graph patch produces materially better drafts. What: implement an AgenticGraphDraftClient conforming to the GraphDraftClient protocol (graph_drafting.py:129) — an internal read-only tool loop (graph context, substring search, decision context; no write tools) that terminates in the existing graph-patch schema. Same provenance stamping (origin_provider/origin_model/origin_prompt_version); consider recording a bounded tool-trace in change-set metadata. Runs ONLY in the background worker, never in request handlers. Selected via settings alongside the existing single-shot providers so it can be rolled back by config.
notes: Explicitly rejected alternative: a new endpoint accepting pre-made proposal patches from external agent harnesses — opens a proposal-injection surface and gives up server-held keys/attribution; revisit only if third-party harnesses must propose drafts. Depends on the structural commit gate and the job runner beads.
title: Agentic graph draft client behind the GraphDraftClient protocol

acceptance_criteria: A user/agent can turn a store:// locator for a file already in OneDrive into a verified ExternalArtifactReference (content_hash minted from a store read) without running the consumer capture client; a later resolve returns 'verified'.
description: artifact_resolution.py only RE-computes and VERIFIES a caller-supplied content_hash (verified/drifted/unresolved); nothing MINTS the initial hash, and /data-stores/{id}/health probes reachability not digest. So attaching a store:// artifact still needs the hash computed somewhere first — fine for the consumer capture clients that hash local bytes, but the consumer lt CLI is a dev package a bench scientist won't run, and the shared core-facility PC (walkthrough gap G7) has no agent. Add a path to register a store-relative artifact and compute its content_hash by reading the declared store with the host's own credentials (e.g. lt store hash store://lab-onedrive/experiments/001/flow/sample.fcs, and/or a server-side hash-on-register that reads via the store adapter). Server-side hashing stays within scope: it reads her declared store with her credential_ref, it does not store bytes.
title: Mint content_hash on store-artifact registration (verified store:// pointer without a local capture client)

description:
GET /data-stores/{store_id} and GET /data-stores/{store_id}/health (src/lab_tracker/routes/data_stores.py) gate access with ensure_project_read(request, store.project_id). Since migration 0050_data_store_group_scope made project_id nullable, group-scoped stores have project_id=None and group_id set. For those stores the check hits membership_role(None, actor) in services/project_authorization.py, which returns None for any actor without global read (no membership on a None project; projects.get(None) is None), raising AuthError. So ordinary group members cannot fetch or health-check their own group's store; only global-read/admin actors can.

Fix: when store.group_id is set, authorize via the group-read path (ensure_group_read -> require_group_read); keep project read for project-scoped stores. Add a regression test with a non-admin group member fetching and health-checking a group-scoped store.

Relates to epic lab-tracker-y5j8, which builds on these endpoints.
title: Group-scoped data stores unreadable by group members via GET/health endpoints

acceptance_criteria: Deleting a node/claim invalidated by a COMMITTED/ARCHIVED pivot, then transitioning that pivot, does not raise; status-only STAGED->COMMITTED with a since-deleted edge ref is handled; tests cover both.
description: invalidates_node_id/invalidates_claim_id use ondelete=SET NULL (db_models.py:834-846; migration 0046:52-59). A PIVOT node must reference exactly one (_ensure_invalidated_refs, exploration_service.py:311-317). delete_exploration_node/delete_claim do plain deletes with no guard, so deleting the target NULLs the pivot ref -> zero refs. update_exploration_node calls _validate_node unconditionally (:273), so any later edit/commit/archive re-runs the exactly-one check and raises; a COMMITTED/ARCHIVED pivot whose target was deleted can be neither re-pointed nor transitioned. Fix: RESTRICT deletion of nodes/claims referenced as invalidates_*, or treat a nulled ref on a non-STAGED pivot as benign, and fast-path status-only transitions to skip re-resolving unchanged refs. Folds related exploration items: cross-type invalidation switch (:253-256), inability to clear optional scalars (None==unchanged), delete-cascades-provenance, and the referential-integrity test gaps.

description:
Make Lab Tracker resilient to local artifacts that move or get renamed, by
recovering them via their content hash when normal dereferencing fails — without
demanding any change to how researchers name or organize their files.

## Essence (the whole want, one sentence)

When a recorded artifact isn't at its stored path, don't give up if the exact
bytes still exist somewhere we're already allowed to look — recover them by
content hash, verified.

## Why (today's behaviour)

`ExternalArtifactReference` is a pointer (`source_system` + `uri` +
`content_hash`), not bytes. `LocalFilesystemResolver.resolve()` recomputes the
digest of whatever it fetched and returns VERIFIED / DRIFTED / UNRESOLVED. When
a local file has simply moved or been renamed it dead-ends at:

    if not os.path.isfile(real_path):
        return _unresolved(ref, detail="Local artifact not found.")

…even though the surviving identity — the `content_hash` — could find the bytes
elsewhere under the already-configured `allowed_roots`.

## Approach: passive, in-place recovery (no user behaviour change)

Recovery must work over files **as researchers already keep them**. That rules
out two tempting designs:

- **Rejected — SHA suffix in the filename.** Pushes content-addressing into the
  namespace the *user* owns; brittle (one user rename breaks it) and invasive.
- **Rejected as a dependency — git-annex / DataLad.** Right *idea* (identity ≠
  name) but wrong *ask*: it wants to own the files (symlinks into an object
  store), only finds content it already ingested, is heavy and Windows-hostile,
  and its payoff scales with commit discipline this user base hasn't built.
  Revisit only if Lab Tracker ever pivots to *owning* data rather than pointing
  at data that lives elsewhere.

Keep identity (the hash) in an index/lookup the user never sees; keep naming the
user's. Build the small core ourselves; reuse the commodity infra we already run
(the SQLAlchemy DB, `file_watch`, and rclone).

## MVP (the floor)

A recovery fallback inside `LocalFilesystemResolver`: on "Local artifact not
found", walk `allowed_roots`, hash candidates, and the first whose digest
matches `ref.content_hash` flows into the existing `_build_resolved()` path and
returns VERIFIED. No new dependency, no schema change, no write path,
side-effect-free. Correctness is free — a hash match *is* the identity and the
existing verify-after still runs; the only new risk is scan *cost*, bounded by a
budget. Behaviour degrades to exactly today's when nothing matches in budget.

See the child tasks for the MVP slice and the deferred (v2+) increments.

## Relevant code

- `src/lab_tracker/artifact_resolution.py` — `LocalFilesystemResolver.resolve`,
  `_within_allowed_roots`, `_hash_and_collect`, `_build_resolved`,
  `registry_from_env`, `LAB_TRACKER_RESOLVER_ALLOWED_ROOTS_ENV`.
- `src/lab_tracker/file_storage.py` — `LocalFileStorageBackend` (sha256 sidecar).
- `src/lab_tracker/file_watch.py` — home for v2 index-freshness / move detection.
- Design context: `docs/external-artifact-resolution-design.md`,
  `docs/data-store-registry-design.md`.
title: Recover lost local artifacts by content hash when dereferencing fails

description: Core of the MVP. In LocalFilesystemResolver.resolve(), where it currently returns _unresolved(ref, detail='Local artifact not found.'), add a fallback: walk the configured allowed_roots, hash candidate files, and the first whose digest matches ref.content_hash is fed into the existing _build_resolved() path -> returns VERIFIED. Reuse _within_allowed_roots, _hash_and_collect, _build_resolved. Read-only and side-effect-free (does NOT rewrite ref.uri). Set ResolvedArtifact.detail to note the bytes were recovered from a path other than the URI. No new dependency, no schema change.
title: Recovery fallback in LocalFilesystemResolver (hash-match over allowed_roots)

description: Keep the walk from being naive. (1) Prioritize candidates whose basename matches the original URI basename (a moved/renamed-parent file usually keeps its name) so the common case is near-free. (2) A hard scan budget (max files and/or max bytes hashed); if no match within budget, return UNRESOLVED exactly as today. Behaviour never gets worse than current.
title: Bound the recovery scan: budget + same-basename priority

description: Recovery reads more of the host than today's resolver, so gate it. Add LAB_TRACKER_RESOLVER_RECOVERY (off by default) read in registry_from_env, alongside LAB_TRACKER_RESOLVER_ALLOWED_ROOTS, plus a default budget constant. Off-by-default keeps the security surface unchanged for anyone who doesn't enable it.
title: Opt-in flag + config wiring for recovery

description: Cover: (a) moved/renamed local file recovers as VERIFIED; (b) budget exhaustion -> UNRESOLVED (degrades to today); (c) a candidate outside allowed_roots is never read/returned; (d) a same-name-but-different-bytes file does NOT falsely resolve (verify-after still gates); (e) flag off -> behaviour identical to today. Mirror existing tests in tests/test_artifact_resolution.py.
title: Tests for content-hash recovery

description: Document the recovery fallback, the flag, and the budget in docs/external-artifact-resolution-design.md, and note the supported behaviour in docs/retained-v1-surface.md. State the invariant: recovery never relaxes the integrity gate (verify-after always runs).
title: Docs: recovery in resolution design + retained surface

description: Optimization over the MVP walk. Maintain a content_hash -> location(s) index (a SQLAlchemy table over the sha256 we already capture) so recovery is an index hit, not a directory walk. Open questions: index storage, staleness/invalidation, scoping to allowed_roots.
title: v2: persistent content_hash -> path index (O(1) recovery)

acceptance_criteria: Installer operations fail closed and redact credentials; test database resources are deterministically closed; high-risk browser flows have automated coverage; MATLAB runtime coverage is organized here or consciously deferred; quality gates remain green.
description: Operational and verification follow-ups from the 2026-07-15 deep review. Harden scheduler/install scripts and replace warning-prone or source-inspection-only confidence with executable lifecycle coverage for databases, browsers, and MATLAB consumers.
design: Prefer thin shell adapters over one tested structured implementation. Never interpolate credentials or destructive scheduler state through unchecked shell text. Keep browser and external-client suites small and risk-focused; enforce a clean warning budget after known resource leaks are removed.
title: Operational safety and executable verification

acceptance_criteria: An unexpected crontab read failure leaves the existing crontab untouched and exits nonzero; spaces, quotes, dollar syntax, and newlines in credentials cannot execute or corrupt configuration; generated requests are valid structured JSON; database URLs are redacted in all logs; cron/launchd/Windows tests cover failure and secret edge cases.
description:
The legacy cron installer treats any crontab -l error as empty input and can overwrite unrelated jobs. The launchd installer writes raw shell assignments then sources them, so credentials containing whitespace or shell syntax can break or execute. The daily-review trigger builds JSON with shell interpolation, and serve-lan.ps1 prints a full credential-bearing database URL.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Make crontab -l fail for a reason other than an absent crontab, then run install-daily-review.sh and observe it writes only the Lab Tracker line.
2. Run the launchd installer with a password containing spaces, quotes, dollar expansion, or command syntax and inspect/source the generated env file.
3. Run serve-lan.ps1 with a credential-bearing database URL and observe the full secret printed.
design: Make shell/PowerShell files thin adapters over one tested Python scheduler/configuration implementation. Distinguish 'no crontab' from read failure, validate schedule/base URL, serialize JSON and environment values structurally, prefer scoped API tokens over admin passwords, and centralize credential-aware URL redaction.
title: Make scheduler installers fail closed and handle credentials structurally

acceptance_criteria: The full pytest suite emits no unclosed-database ResourceWarning under normal and xdist execution; helper resources close after passing and failing tests; unexpected ResourceWarning is treated as an error; any retained third-party warning has an owner and narrow documented filter; coverage remains stable.
description: The full suite passes but emits 139 warnings, mostly ResourceWarning for unclosed SQLite connections. tests/api_helpers.repository_backed_api creates an engine/session and stores them on api._test_resources without deterministic cleanup, and the helper is used broadly. Persistent warning noise can mask future resource and dependency regressions.
design: Convert repository-backed test APIs to yield fixtures/context managers or register finalizers that close sessions and dispose engines under success and failure, including xdist. Resolve the Starlette/httpx deprecation or document a narrowly scoped temporary filter, then fail on new unexpected warnings.
title: Close test database resources and enforce a clean warning budget

acceptance_criteria: CI executes browser tests for prefixed native links, logout/account-switch with queued capture, one offline/service-worker replay, rapid graph-draft route change, and one media/share-target fallback; failures retain useful traces; the suite is documented and reliably repeatable locally.
description: Frontend tests run in jsdom and service-worker tests largely inspect source text. Browser-critical behavior such as native prefixed links, login/logout with queued captures, service-worker/offline replay, route races, and browser media capability fallback is not executed in CI despite Playwright being installed.
design: Add a small deterministic Playwright suite against a disposable local API/app. Cover only behavior that jsdom cannot validate; keep physical-device smoke testing separate. Seed minimal data, avoid external services, capture traces on failure, and make CI runtime bounded.
title: Add a risk-focused Playwright browser lifecycle suite

acceptance_criteria: Frontend watch output includes source maps and React development diagnostics; production build remains minified and deterministic; App.test.jsx retains only shell-level journeys and shrinks materially; feature tests own their scenarios; lint, frontend tests, and generated-bundle checks pass.

title: Restore development-mode frontend diagnostics and split the shell test change magnet

acceptance_criteria: A live provider call cannot be reclaimed before its configured timeout without an explicit expired-owner transition; stale workers cannot save or complete after ownership changes; scheduling and generation recovery are idempotent; concurrent Postgres tests exercise reclaim and stale completion; source context has a documented aggregate budget; focused/full backend gates and relevant frontend tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented provider-timeout-aware fenced generation and batch recovery with CAS ownership, aggregate context budgeting, SQLite/Postgres race coverage, and green release gates.
description: The divergent onboarding release added 300-second generation and 600-second batch-run leases, but configured provider calls can run for 5,400 seconds and observed work has exceeded 15 minutes. Without heartbeat, ownership tokens, or compare-and-swap completion, a live request can be reclaimed and an older completion can overwrite the newer attempt. Rebuild interrupted generation and scheduling recovery on current main before porting starter-question onboarding. Scope full source text to starter/note drafting or enforce an aggregate batch-context budget; do not globally expand 100-note batches to roughly 6.4M characters.
design: Use provider-timeout-aware lease durations plus owner tokens and repository-level compare-and-swap/fencing for renew/complete/fail transitions. Add heartbeats where appropriate, reject stale owners, preserve idempotent change-set semantics, and cover real Postgres concurrent claims. Stack after the graph-schema repair PR; stack starter-question policy/UI only after this recovery contract is proven.
title: Redesign graph-draft recovery with provider-aware fenced leases

description: GET /portfolio/summary re-introduces the per-project query-loop and unbounded-payload anti-pattern epic 4bk targets, and does not meet the isj acceptance criterion to bound payload/pagination. Per-project N+1 sources (portfolio.py, now 324 lines): (1) query_projects(limit=None) loads every project then scopes/paginates in Python (portfolio.py:62-70). (2) _latest_activity_at loads ALL rows of nine entity types per project just to compute one max(timestamp) (portfolio.py:169-190). (3) _count_statuses issues one query per status value with a wasted limit=1 row (portfolio.py:152-166). (4) _owners_for_project runs query_project_memberships per project (portfolio.py:201-214). (5) _triage_flags_for_project (added by 80i after this bead) runs four more unbounded per-project loads - query_datasets/analyses/claims/goals (portfolio.py:244-300). That is ~20 repo round-trips per project, ~1000 per default 50-project page. ACCEPTANCE: the SQL pushdown MUST preserve vkcj.2's group-before-paginate fix (portfolio.py:68-70 builds all group summaries from the full visible list, then paginates GROUPS with total=#groups); a naive project-level LIMIT/OFFSET pushdown would reintroduce the vkcj.2 split-groups/meta.total bug.
design: Pass accessible_project_ids as WHERE project_id IN (:ids) (admin None short-circuit = no filter) plus LIMIT/OFFSET and use the SQL COUNT for total. Replace _latest_activity_at row loads with select(func.max(created_at/updated_at)) grouped by project_id over all visible projects (existing (project_id, created_at) indexes make this index-cheap). Replace per-status queries with SELECT status, COUNT(*) GROUP BY project_id, status per entity type (or at minimum limit=0). Collapses the endpoint to a small fixed number of aggregate queries independent of project count and size.
notes: Net-new instance not in the 4bk.1 checklist (portfolio.py landed 2026-06-15, after the 4bk epic 2026-06-12). Blocked by 4bk.8: extract the shared visible-projects prefix first so the pushdown happens in one place. Body reconciled 2026-06-17 - re-anchored line numbers and added the 80i triage-flag and _owners_for_project N+1 loops (portfolio.py grew 167->324 lines via sls/769.1/769.2/80i/vkcj after this bead was filed).
title: Push portfolio summary scoping, pagination, and aggregates into SQL

description: portfolio_summary and list_projects still share, verbatim, the visible-projects PREFIX: validate_pagination -> query_projects(limit=None, offset=0) -> filter_project_scoped_items (portfolio.py:60-67 == projects.py:95-101), doubling the surface the 4bk SQL-pushdown must migrate and risking divergence. The blocks diverge AFTER that prefix: since vkcj.2, portfolio_summary builds per-project summaries, groups them, and paginates GROUPS (portfolio.py:68-70), while list_projects paginates the PROJECT list (projects.py:102). So extract a helper that returns the UNPAGINATED visible-project list - e.g. visible_projects(request, repository, status) -> list[Project] - into routes/shared.py and call it from both: list_projects paginates the result, portfolio_summary groups then paginates. (The originally proposed paginated_visible_projects(..., limit, offset) signature no longer fits portfolio_summary's group pagination.)
notes: Blocks the portfolio SQL-pushdown bead 4bk.7 under epic 4bk (extract the shared prefix before the pushdown). Rescoped + repriced to P2 2026-06-17: vkcj.2's group-before-paginate fix made the old "duplicates the paginate block verbatim" premise stale - only the query+filter prefix is now shared, so the helper returns the unpaginated visible list rather than a paginated page.

description:
Write the decision-complete public application profile that separates structural classes from controlled concepts and qualified relationships. This is the semantic contract for subsequent exporter work, not an internal model redesign.

## Acceptance Criteria
The profile fixes the class-admission rule, exact core and extension class tables, concept schemes and predicates, qualified-edge rule, mapping for every exported record and relationship, Project exclusion, ARA boundary, and additive compatibility policy, leaving no semantic or rollout decision to implementation.
design: The core record classes are ResearchQuestion, Dataset, Claim, Note, Visualization, Goal, and ExplorationNode as subclasses of prov:Entity, plus Analysis and AcquisitionSession as subclasses of prov:Activity. Project is excluded until it has a first-class export. Person and SoftwareAgent use their single standard PROV classes. ClaimRelation, GoalLink, and a qualified question link are resources only where edge role, outcome, status, slot, or provenance metadata requires reification. AraArtifact, AraLayer, and ForensicBinding belong to a separately declared ARA extension; EntityVersion belongs to the provenance extension. Question type, session type, goal type, exploration kind, status, origin, role, outcome, link state, and relation kind are URI-addressed concepts, not subclasses. Existing literal fields remain during this epic and may only be removed in a future explicit profile-major change.

acceptance_criteria: All child correctness issues are fixed or explicitly deferred; offline jobs cannot cross identities; stale responses cannot mutate the wrong resource; partial mutations are accurately reported; frontend lint/tests and targeted browser coverage pass.
description: Findings from the 2026-07-15 ArjanCodes-style deep review of the React/PWA surface. Protect resource identity, authorization context, queued-job ownership, and mutation outcomes across route changes, concurrent requests, logout/account switching, and offline replay.
design: Model workflows with resource-keyed state and operation-local pending/error results. Persist job ownership but never bearer credentials. Keep server authorization as the backstop while ensuring the UI does not offer or execute actions based on stale project or route state. Extract controllers only after behavior is covered.
title: Frontend workflow integrity and offline identity

acceptance_criteria: IndexedDB contains no bearer token for newly queued jobs; logout cannot drain with the old credential; account B cannot submit account A's job; matching-user login can intentionally resume its own queue; migration behavior for legacy token-bearing jobs is safe and tested; offline/service-worker tests pass.
description:
The IndexedDB upload queue persists the enqueue-time bearer token and may fall back to it when no live token is supplied. Logout can therefore be followed by an upload using the old still-valid credential; after account switching, a new user's token can submit a prior user's queued job and misattribute the capture.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Sign in as user A, enqueue an offline upload, and inspect IndexedDB to find A's bearer token stored with the job.
2. Log out and allow the retry effect to drain without a live token; observe fallback to the persisted token.
3. Alternatively sign in as B and observe the queued A job can be submitted using B's live token.
design: Persist a stable job-owner identity and non-secret request data, never credentials. Drain only with an active session whose identity matches the job owner. Quarantine or explicitly hand off jobs after logout/account switch; do not silently rewrite attribution.
title: Bind offline upload jobs to an identity without persisting bearer tokens

acceptance_criteria: Out-of-order A/B membership responses cannot change B's access; direct-linked resources use their own project_id regardless of dashboard selection; controls are disabled while access is unknown; contributor/owner/admin scenarios and stale-request regression tests pass.
description:
AppShell derives contribution/management permissions from members of the mutable dashboard-selected project. Membership requests are not sequenced or cancelled and previous membership remains during loading, so a late response can overwrite the current project and direct-linked question/note/session views can receive permissions for the wrong project.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Select project A and delay its members response.
2. Select project B and let B's members response complete first.
3. Release A's response and observe it overwrites membership used to derive B's controls.
4. Open a direct-linked resource from another project and observe controls still use the dashboard-selected project.
design: Create one useProjectAccess(projectId) boundary returning explicit loading/unknown/allowed states, keyed to each resource's own project_id. Sequence or abort requests, clear stale membership immediately, and keep the server as the authorization backstop.
title: Key frontend project access to the loaded resource and reject stale membership responses

acceptance_criteria: Rapid A→B route changes cannot display A as B or send any mutation to A; late A responses are ignored; actions remain disabled until the loaded ID matches the route; regression tests cover navigation during loading and an in-flight mutation.
description:
GraphDraftDetailCard neither clears changeSet nor rejects stale load responses when changeSetId changes. The previous draft remains actionable while the next route loads, a late old response can overwrite the new state, and mutation handlers target changeSet.change_set_id rather than proving it matches the route.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open graph draft A and, before or after it loads, navigate the same component to draft B while requests are in flight.
2. Observe A remains displayed/actionable or a late A response overwrites B.
3. Trigger a mutation and observe the handler targets changeSet.change_set_id rather than a state proven to match the route.
design: Use an abort/request-generation pattern at the resource gateway, reset route-scoped state immediately, and couple command eligibility to loadedResourceId === routeId. Preserve unsaved-edit UX deliberately rather than through stale component state.
title: Prevent stale graph-draft route state from mutating the wrong draft

acceptance_criteria: Accept all never reports blanket success after a partial failure and exposes exactly which operations changed; nested mutations cannot clear another command's pending state; duplicate submissions are prevented for non-idempotent commands; buttons reflect local pending state; focused graph-draft/note tests pass.
description:
saveOperation catches errors without returning failure, so Accept all continues and later successes can overwrite an earlier error while leaving a partially accepted draft. A shared application-wide busy boolean is also set and cleared by unrelated or nested operations, allowing duplicate non-idempotent submissions while work remains in flight.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In Accept all, make an early saveOperation request fail and a later one succeed.
2. Observe processing continues, the later success can replace the error flash, and the draft is only partially accepted.
3. Start overlapping/nested mutations and observe one finally block clears the shared busy flag while another request remains in flight.
design: Introduce operation-local command state with execute, pending, and typed Result/error. Stop or aggregate Accept all outcomes explicitly; add per-command in-flight guards. Use a counter only for optional global activity indication. Consider a server batch command only if atomic acceptance is a domain requirement.
title: Replace ambient busy/error state with explicit frontend mutation results

acceptance_criteria: Click, copy, modifier-click, and open-in-new-tab resolve identically under root and /lab-tracker prefixes; external links remain untouched; a component-level routing test covers the rendered href and intercepted navigation.
description:

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Serve the app below a prefix such as /lab-tracker/app.
2. Render an AppLink to /app/graph.
3. Normal click uses prefixed programmatic navigation, but copy the href or open in a new tab and observe navigation to the unprefixed root path.
design: Resolve the application path once and use the same canonical URL for href and navigation. Keep external URLs and browser-native link semantics intact.
title: Resolve AppLink href and programmatic navigation through one prefix rule

acceptance_criteria: Representative project, dataset, note, graph-draft, and auth responses are statically described and runtime-validated; malformed 2xx envelopes produce one explicit contract error rather than null/empty data; raw fetch/envelope parsing is not duplicated in feature controllers; lint/tests and generated-contract drift checks pass.
description: The centralized apiRequest layer converts malformed successful envelopes to null or empty lists while downstream components trust raw shapes. Backend contract drift can therefore look like an empty result in one path and a render crash in another.
design: Define domain gateways such as projects.list and datasets.get using generated OpenAPI TypeScript types or checked JSDoc plus runtime validators at the network boundary. Invalid 2xx payloads must fail loudly as typed contract errors; components consume validated domain DTOs.
title: Add typed, runtime-validated frontend API gateways

acceptance_criteria: Login, token refresh, and logout remain usable when storage get/set/remove each throw; degraded persistence is observable but does not crash the application; normal persistence behavior is unchanged; tests cover quota and security failures.
description:
Initial auth token reads catch unavailable localStorage, but synchronization writes and removals are unguarded. Quota, privacy-mode, or SecurityError failures after a successful login can escape into the top-level error boundary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the app with localStorage.setItem or removeItem throwing SecurityError or QuotaExceededError.
2. Complete a successful login, token refresh, or logout.
3. Observe the unguarded synchronization write escapes to the application error boundary.
design: Provide one injected auth-storage adapter with symmetric read/write/remove error handling and an in-memory fallback. Surface degraded persistence without discarding a valid live session, and keep logout semantics explicit.
title: Hide auth persistence behind a resilient storage adapter

acceptance_criteria: answers_question_ids round-trips model<->DB; create_claim (API + MCP) accepts it; service rejects question ids outside the claim's project; project_graph emits claim->question 'answers' edge in full+evidence views; presentation manifest validates with claim_question_answers and the vocabulary test passes; deck JSON uses the answers edge and slide 16 no longer says a figure 'addresses' a question; uv run pytest -q and ruff clean.
description:
Claims have no direct link to the question they answer. Today a claim joins the question hierarchy only transitively via supporting datasets (dataset_question_*), which is ambiguous when a claim draws on datasets addressing different questions. This blocks the questions-first query 'what does the lab currently claim about question X?' and forces the research-group deck to imply a figure/claim->question relationship its edges cannot encode.

Add a plain claim->question 'answers' link: Claim.answers_question_ids: list[UUID]. Verdict (supports/refutes) is inferred from the claim's own statement/status; no outcome_status on the link (decided over the outcome-bearing variant).

Vertical: domain model + ClaimInput; claim_questions association table (mirror claim_datasets/dataset_question_links); mappers; sqlalchemy repository load/save; alembic 0011; schemas ClaimCreate/Update + response; claim_service validation (question in project); routes/claims; MCP create_claim + mcp_api_client; provenance JSON-LD; project_graph edge (claim_question_answers, label 'answers'); presentation_graphs PROJECT_GRAPH_RELATIONSHIPS; the research-group deck JSON + prose; tests across the stack.
design: Relationship string: claim_question_answers; edge direction claim->question; label 'answers'; emitted from project_graph._add_evidence_edges. Storage: claim_questions(claim_id FK->claims CASCADE, question_id FK->questions). No outcome column. Cardinality: list (a claim may answer multiple questions). Surface: retained-v1 core (questions + evidence-linked claims).
title: Add claim→question 'answers' relationship (plain answers_question_ids)

description: A PI deploys Lab Tracker with many projects and project-scoped trainees. Today there is no container above Project, no real notion of people (created_by is a free string; the only cross-project tier is global ADMIN), and oversight requires being a global admin. This epic adds an organizing-edge layer — a Lab/project-group container, supervision and ownership edges, and read-only portfolio/lab-health views — without becoming an identity provider, HR system, or grants-management product. Build-vs-buy moat preserved: identity stays offloadable; we own the semantic edges.
design:
CONCEPT: Add the three semantic edges no identity provider models — group ownership, supervision, attribution — onto the existing model; route PI oversight through accessible_project_ids(). No org-chart/HR/IdP/grants-management.

NEW: project_groups (kind=lab) + group_memberships (reuse VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR/OWNER enum); supervision_edges (dated, own table keyed by user_id, NOT a users column); shadow FK created_by_user_id/executed_by_user_id (additive; string stays, dual-written).
CHANGE: goals.project_id nullable + GoalLink EntityType.PROJECT slot (enum value already exists, models.py:155); accessible_project_ids()/membership_role() group-aware.
REUSE: prov:Agent -> prov:Person/wasAttributedTo/actedOnBehalfOf (export-only); project_graph, decision_context (stays single-project), graph-draft human review, goals.

ACCESS CONTRACT (2.1, asymmetric): group OWNER inherits OWNER on every child project (PI oversight w/o global admin); group VIEWER/CONTRIBUTOR inherit NOTHING unless an explicit per-group group_read_all flag (default false). Direct project membership resolves first; admin short-circuit and >=1-owner-per-project guard untouched.

BOUNDARY: every new edge points at the offloadable users table but adds NO domain column to users itself. Aggregations (portfolio/lab-health) read only over the in-house question/claim/goal graph — not a metrics/ELN dashboard.

PHASES: 0 read-only portfolio (zero schema) -> 1 group container + group-aware access -> 2 attribution FK (isolated) -> 3 spanning goals + supervision + PROV-O people -> 4 offboarding export + ownership reassignment. Each additive, single Alembic head.
notes:
Source: multi-agent design pass (2026-06-15), grounded in db_models.py, services/project_authorization.py, auth.py, provenance.py, docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md, docs/retained-v1-surface.md.
DEFERRED per PI decision (2026-06-15): co-PI / cross-lab / multi-parented projects. Single-parent projects.group_id stands; co-PI handled later by direct per-project membership + goal-level overlap if demand proves it.
NOTE: per-trainee attribution has signal only once multi-user auth (auth_enabled=True) is in use; default local mode collapses all rows to one ADMIN user.
title: PI information organization: project groups, people-edges, and portfolio views

acceptance_criteria: GET /portfolio/summary returns 200 for a project with a graph change set on SQLite; regression test added; change_set_from_model normalized.
description: GET /portfolio/summary returns HTTP 500 for any accessible project that has a graph change set. _latest_activity_at (src/lab_tracker/routes/portfolio.py:122-143) builds a candidate list of tz-aware datetimes (project plus eight entity mappers normalize via as_utc) then calls max(), but change_set_from_model (src/lab_tracker/sqlalchemy_repository_parts/graph_drafts.py:199-200) returns created_at/updated_at WITHOUT as_utc normalization. On SQLite (all tests and local dev) DateTime(timezone=True) returns tz-naive datetimes, so max() over mixed aware/naive raises TypeError. Postgres masks it. Existing tests never create a change set, so it is latent.
design: Defensively normalize each non-None timestamp with as_utc inside _activity_timestamps before max(); additionally normalize change_set_from_model for parity with the other eight mappers (the underlying c1u.5 fix). Add a portfolio route test that creates a graph change set and asserts 200 + correct last_activity_at.
notes: Net-new portfolio-specific surface; cross-links lab-tracker-c1u.5 (mapper normalization). Fixing c1u.5 alone resolves the crash but not the route-level guard or the test.
title: Fix portfolio last_activity_at tz-aware/naive HTTP 500 + graph-change-set regression test

Device enrollment + token is effectively the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628), a fully standardized flow. Maintaining bespoke auth is high-risk and off-core. Candidates: FastAPI-Users (library altitude, likely sweet spot for single-lab deploys), or an IdP such as Keycloak/Authentik (self-host) or Clerk/Auth0 (SaaS) if multi-tenant. Decide whether to offload and at what altitude (library vs service).
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: Lab Tracker keeps project membership/role edges (which user has which role on which project) in the graph, but delegates credential storage, session/token issuance, and the device grant to the chosen provider/library. Avoid running a full IdP unless multi-tenant requirements justify the operational weight.
title: Decision: offload auth/RBAC instead of maintaining bespoke identity
