title: Deep review 2026-06-19 follow-up

description:
0023 runs `UPDATE goal_links SET slot = '' WHERE slot IS NULL` and then makes `slot` NOT NULL. The unique constraint `uq_goal_links_goal_entity_relation_slot` over `(goal_id, entity_type, entity_id, relation, slot)` has existed since 0022; because SQLite/Postgres treat NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE constraints, two goal_links rows that share goal/entity/relation but both have slot=NULL are legal at rest. The moment 0023's UPDATE sets both to '' it violates that unique constraint and the whole upgrade aborts. Commit 4ac4ddb ('move goal link dedupe to forward migration', bead rjg1.13) REMOVED the `_dedupe_unslotted_goal_links()` call that previously ran inside 0023 *before* this UPDATE, and put it in a new revision 0041 that sits LATER in the chain (0023 -> 0024 -> ... -> 0040 -> 0041). The dedupe therefore can never run before the statement that fails. I reproduced this end-to-end: seeding a DB at rev 0022 with two NULL-slot duplicate links and running `alembic upgrade head` fails with `IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: goal_links.goal_id, goal_links.entity_type, goal_links.entity_id, goal_links.relation, goal_links.slot` at the 0023 UPDATE. Consequence: any self-hosted DB currently at version <= 0022 that contains duplicate unslotted goal_links (possible in older DBs created before the slot default, or via direct SQL/imports) becomes permanently un-upgradeable, and since the app runs `alembic upgrade head` on startup this is a hard, data-blocking outage with no in-product recovery.

Fix: Restore the dedupe so it executes before 0023's slot-normalizing UPDATE. Simplest: re-add the `_dedupe_unslotted_goal_links()` DELETE as the first statement of 0023.upgrade() (before the UPDATE). If keeping a separate forward-only revision is desired for already-migrated DBs, that is fine to ALSO keep at 0041 for idempotency, but the in-0023 dedupe is required to keep stuck-at-0022 DBs upgradeable. The DELETE is already idempotent (it only removes ROW_NUMBER()>1 duplicates), so running it in both places is safe.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding migrations-1
title: Goal-link dedupe runs AFTER the migration it must precede; DBs with duplicate NULL-slot links can no longer upgrade past 0023

description:
export_user_records()/_collect_records() return repository.records_attributed_to_user(), which yields a RecordExportRecords containing only questions, datasets, analyses, claims, claim_edges, and notes (models.py:876-883 has no sessions/visualizations fields). Sessions (project-scoped, created_by attributed; db_models.py:544-566) and Visualizations are first-class retained-v1 entities (docs/retained-v1-surface.md:39-45) and ARE attributed/reassigned by reassign() (ownership.py:60-64,77). The offboarding guard's _attributed_record_project_ids() (project_service.py:644-654) reads the same RecordExportRecords and likewise ignores sessions/visualizations. Consequences: (1) the two offboarding-release mechanisms diverge -- reassign moves session/viz attribution, but export does NOT preserve them, so an admin who 'export-then-revokes' loses the departing user's session and visualization provenance; (2) a departing user whose only attributable artifacts are sessions or visualizations passes _ensure_offboarding_records_released() with no export at all, then is revoked, leaving those rows attributed to a removed member. For an app whose entire purpose is preserving research reasoning, this is a real data-preservation defect.

Fix: Add sessions and visualizations to RecordExportRecords and to repository.records_attributed_to_user() (using SessionModel.created_by/created_by_user_id and VisualizationModel.created_by/created_by_user_id with the project_filter), include them in _record_counts() and in _project_ids_for_records(), and add their project_ids to _attributed_record_project_ids() in project_service so the offboarding guard blocks revoke until they are exported or reassigned. Add a regression test asserting a user with only a session/visualization is blocked from revoke until export.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding services-authz-1
title: Per-user record export and offboarding guard silently omit sessions and visualizations

description:
delete_session removes the session and (via the acquisition_outputs.session_id ondelete=CASCADE FK at db_models.py:602) silently cascade-deletes every registered acquisition output, with no reference check. Meanwhile a dataset created by promote_operational_session_to_dataset records the session in commit_manifest.source_session_id, which is persisted as a plain String(36) column (db_models.py:208) with NO foreign key. So you can delete an operational session after it has been promoted to a committed dataset: the dataset keeps a source_session_id pointing at a now-nonexistent session, and the acquisition outputs that back that committed dataset's file manifest vanish. For a tool whose stated purpose is preserving research provenance, this silently breaks the provenance chain for irreplaceable committed data. Contrast delete_dataset (_ensure_dataset_can_be_deleted) and delete_question (_ensure_question_not_referenced), which both refuse deletion while referenced. test_session_routes.py only covers deleting an unreferenced session, so the gap is untested.

Fix: Before deleting a session, query datasets in the session's project (or add a repository lookup keyed on manifest_source_session_id) and raise ValidationError if any committed/non-staged dataset's commit_manifest.source_session_id == session_id, mirroring the reference guards on dataset/question deletion. Also consider guarding sessions that still have acquisition outputs. Add a regression test that promotes a session to a committed dataset and asserts the session cannot be deleted.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding services-crud-1
title: delete_session destroys provenance: no guard against deleting a session referenced as a committed dataset's source_session_id

description:
In scan(), `_stable_fingerprint(file_path)` is called for EVERY file on EVERY poll BEFORE the cheap size/mtime short-circuit at lines 80-85. `_stable_fingerprint` (line 125-138) calls `_hash_file` (line 128), which reads the entire file and computes SHA-256. The size/mtime comparison against the cached fingerprint that would skip unchanged files only happens AFTER the full hash has already been computed. For the watcher's actual use case (instrument output directories that can hold many multi-GB files), this means the process re-reads and SHA-256s every file on the watch tree at every interval (default 1s in run(), line 105). This is an O(total bytes) cost per poll and will saturate disk I/O / CPU and effectively make the watcher unusable on large acquisition datasets. The cheap stat check is meant to gate the expensive hash, but the order is inverted.

Fix: Restructure scan() to stat first and hash only when needed: read `path.stat()`, compare size+mtime against `self._fingerprints[file_path]`; if both match a previously-registered fingerprint, `continue` without hashing. Only when size/mtime differ (or no prior fingerprint) compute the stable hash. Keep the stability double-stat inside the hash branch. This preserves change detection while bounding per-poll cost to a stat() per file for the steady state.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding storage-1
title: Acquisition watcher re-hashes every file on every poll (expensive hash runs before the cheap stat check)

description:
The offline upload queue replays capture POSTs to /notes/quick-capture and /notes/upload-file with no idempotency token, and the server (routes/notes.py:86-162 -> upload_note_raw) performs no dedup. Two failure modes produce duplicates: (1) a network error thrown by fetch AFTER the server already created the note but before the response reached the phone (flaky LAN/Wi-Fi, dropped connection) leaves the item queued (results.stillQueued.push at line 230) and it is retried on the next drain; (2) any 5xx (e.g. a 502/504 from a reverse proxy issued after the note was committed) hits the else branch at line 265-267 and is likewise retried. Each replay creates a brand-new note row AND a new on-disk raw asset. This is exactly the flaky-network scenario the queue exists for, so duplicate staged notes (and wasted irreplaceable-capture storage) are a realistic outcome that also pollutes the daily batch-draft window.

Fix: Generate a client-side idempotency key per enqueued item (e.g. a UUID stored in the IndexedDB record at enqueue time) and send it as a form field / header on every retry. On the server, add a unique constraint on (project_id, client_capture_id) for notes and have upload_note_raw look up an existing note by that key, returning the existing note (200) instead of inserting a duplicate when the key is already present.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-concurrency-1
title: Capture upload retry creates duplicate notes (no idempotency key)

description:
run_due_graph_draft_batches selects due settings via list_due (graph_batches.py:184-194, a plain SELECT on enabled AND next_run_at<=now) and only advances next_run_at AFTER each project's run completes (line 624-633). The run itself includes a slow LLM call, so the due window stays open for seconds. The whole thing runs inside one request-managed transaction (RepositoryUnitOfWork does not commit when request-managed, base.py:79-80), so the RUNNING GraphDraftBatchRun row created at graph_draft_service.py:519-520 is never committed mid-run and is invisible to any concurrent caller. Two concurrent POSTs to /batches/run-due (or one cron whose interval is shorter than the run, or an admin manually triggering while cron runs) will both see the same project as due and both invoke run_graph_draft_batch_for_project. Because each invocation computes window_end from its own current_time, the two batch_keys can differ, so both runs execute a full LLM batch draft and write separate change sets / runs for the same notes; when batch_keys do match, the loser hits the uncaught uq_graph_draft_batch_runs_batch_key IntegrityError and 500s.

Fix: Claim each due settings row atomically before running: issue an UPDATE ... SET next_run_at=<next> WHERE settings_id=? AND next_run_at=<observed> and only run the project if rowcount==1 (advance the schedule up front, not after). Alternatively serialize run-due with a single-flight guard / advisory lock so only one invocation processes due projects at a time, and commit the RUNNING row before the LLM call so concurrent callers can see it.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-concurrency-2
title: Scheduled batch runner has no overlap/double-run protection

description:
LocalNoteStorage.store_stream writes the captured bytes directly to the final path via path.open('wb') (line 62-70) and store/_write_bytes uses path.write_bytes (line 105-108); neither fsyncs the file nor uses a temp-file + os.replace. The note DB row (which references the storage_id) is committed by SQLite, but the asset bytes may not be durably flushed to disk, so after a power loss the DB can claim a note exists while its raw asset is truncated or missing. The non-atomic write also leaves a partial/orphaned file at the final path on a crash mid-write. Notably the sibling dataset/visualization backend (file_storage.py:_atomic_write_bytes and store_stream lines 164-175) already does fsync + os.replace, so the capture path -- which holds the often-only copy of an irreplaceable phone capture -- has strictly weaker durability than the dataset path.

Fix: Mirror LocalFileStorageBackend: write to a NamedTemporaryFile in the same directory, handle.flush() + os.fsync(handle.fileno()), then os.replace onto the final path, cleaning up the temp file on failure. This gives atomic publish and crash durability for note raw assets.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-concurrency-4
title: Note raw-asset capture writes are not fsync'd or atomically replaced

description:
goal_links reference targets by plain (entity_type, entity_id) columns with NO foreign key (db_models.py:854-855), so they are never removed by DB cascade and must be pruned in application code. delete_analysis (analysis_service.py:248-254) calls remove_goal_links_to_entity for the ANALYSIS only, then deletes the analysis row. The DB then cascade-deletes that analysis's visualizations (visualizations.analysis_id ForeignKey ondelete='CASCADE', db_models.py:877). Any goal_link whose target is (VISUALIZATION, viz_id) for those cascade-deleted visualizations is left behind, pointing at a row that no longer exists. VISUALIZATION is a valid goal target (models.py:248). Consequence: goals silently accumulate dangling links to deleted figures; goal-scope invariants (a projectless goal must retain a real target) can be violated, and downstream goal/portfolio queries surface phantom entities. Note the project-delete path is correct here (remove_goal_links_to_project_contents enumerates visualizations, goal_link_cleanup.py:38-53) - only the direct analysis-delete path has the gap, which is exactly the kind of inconsistency that hides in review.

Fix: In delete_analysis, before deleting, enumerate the analysis's visualizations (repository.query_visualizations(... ) filtered to analysis_id, or the existing viz lookup) and build a target set that includes both (ANALYSIS, analysis_id) and (VISUALIZATION, viz_id) for each child, then call remove_goal_links_to_targets(repository, targets) once. Add a regression test that links a goal to a visualization, deletes the parent analysis, and asserts the goal_link is gone.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-integrity-1
title: Deleting an analysis orphans goal_links pointing at its cascade-deleted visualizations

description:
All integration fixtures build SQLite URLs (sqlite_database_url / migrated_sqlite_database_url, conftest.py:100-121) and there is no Postgres-backed test path, yet CLAUDE.md and the skills describe a 'Postgres live runtime' as the deployment target. The cross-cutting integrity behaviors that differ between the two engines are precisely the ones this area cares about: ON DELETE cascade/RESTRICT ordering within multi-child cascades, FK enforcement semantics, the REPEATABLE READ isolation branch in the Dolt export (dolt_mirror.py:86-87, which is skipped on SQLite and therefore never exercised), default-NO-ACTION vs RESTRICT timing for datasets.primary_question_id / sessions.primary_question_id (db_models.py:194-198, 559-562), and JSON/boolean column round-tripping. Consequence: a schema or delete-ordering change could pass CI on SQLite and corrupt or fail on the actual Postgres deployment, with no automated signal.

Fix: Add a Postgres-parametrized variant of the integration fixtures (e.g. a marker/env-gated session that runs migrations + a representative subset of the cascade/delete/export tests against a Postgres container), at minimum covering project-cascade delete with full entity tree, the Dolt export REPEATABLE READ path, and FK enforcement. Run it in CI.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding sweep-integrity-3
title: Entire test suite runs only on SQLite while production targets Postgres - cross-backend FK/cascade/isolation behavior is untested

description:
pytest emits SAWarning at src/lab_tracker/dolt_mirror.py:74: 'Cannot correctly sort tables; there are unresolvable cycles between tables graph_change_sets, notes, usually caused by mutually dependent foreign key constraints. Foreign key constraints involving these tables will not be considered; this warning may raise an error in a future release.' The Dolt mirror may order/handle graph_change_sets and notes incorrectly during export, and a future SQLAlchemy upgrade turns this warning into a hard error.

Fix: Break the FK cycle (e.g. use_alter=True on one of the mutually-dependent FKs) or give dolt_mirror an explicit table ordering instead of relying on SQLAlchemy's topological sort.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding gates-2
title: Dolt mirror: unresolvable FK cycle between graph_change_sets and notes

description:
The serve subcommand accepts an arbitrary --host (default 127.0.0.1, which is safe) but does nothing to reconcile the bind interface with the auth posture. By default environment='local' (config.py:22) and Settings.is_auth_enabled() returns False for 'local' (config.py:54-57), so the auth middleware short-circuits and grants every request a full ADMIN local context (middleware.py:93-95, local_auth_context()). A user following the 'open to my lab' instinct who runs `lab_tracker serve --host 0.0.0.0` therefore publishes a fully unauthenticated, admin-privileged app onto the LAN, with read/write/delete over all irreplaceable research data, and the CLI prints no warning. serve_app only special-cases 0.0.0.0/:: for the *browser* URL (cli.py:80) and never checks whether binding a non-loopback interface while auth is disabled is dangerous.

Fix: In serve_app (or main()), detect a non-loopback host (anything other than 127.0.0.1/::1/localhost) and, when settings.is_auth_enabled() is False, refuse to start (raise SystemExit with a clear message) or require an explicit override flag like --insecure-allow-lan. At minimum emit a prominent stderr warning naming the exposed interface and the disabled-auth state. Read get_settings() in serve_app to make this decision before uvicorn.run.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding bootstrap-cli-1
title: serve --host 0.0.0.0 exposes an unauthenticated admin app to the LAN with no warning

description:
upsert_note derives an idempotency 'marker' from only the first non-blank line of the content (first_line_marker) and, if any existing note in the project shares that marker, returns the existing note WITHOUT sending the new content (line 630-632). Two genuinely different notes that happen to begin with the same heading/first line (e.g. '# Notes', '## Results', a shared template header) collapse: the caller believes the note was written but the new body is silently dropped and never persisted. This is the documented marker-based contract, but it is a sharp edge for irreplaceable lab notes and the test at tests/test_lab_tracker_client.py:103-107 demonstrates the silent drop ('Updated body that should not duplicate'). There is no signal to the caller distinguishing 'created' from 'matched existing and discarded your content'.

Fix: Make the outcome observable and the marker robust: either return a flag/field indicating reuse-vs-create (so callers can detect a no-op write), or require a stronger marker (e.g. an explicit idempotency key / content hash) rather than the bare first line. At minimum, document on the method that a first-line collision discards content, and consider warning/raising when an existing match's body differs from the supplied content.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding consumer-client-3
title: upsert_note silently discards new content when first non-blank line collides

description:
rollup_usage_events_before() always INSERTs a fresh-UUID UsageEventRollupModel for every bucket (session.add at line 283), never merging into an existing bucket. The retention endpoint POST /usage-events/retention/run uses a sliding cutoff (now - 365 days), so events from a single calendar day get rolled up across multiple daily runs, producing repeated buckets for the same (day, verb, resource_type, project_id, actor_role, principal_type, surface, outcome) key. The uq_usage_event_rollup_bucket UNIQUE constraint is supposed to prevent this, but it does NOT fire because the bucket includes nullable dimensions (project_id, actor_role, principal_type, surface) and SQL treats NULLs as distinct in UNIQUE constraints. Most usage events have a NULL project_id, so the common case silently inserts a duplicate bucket instead of raising. I reproduced this: two events on the same day rolled up in two runs yield two separate rollup rows each with event_count=1. Consequence: usage analytics become silently inflated/double-counted over time; aggregations over rollups overstate activity, with no error surfaced.

Fix: In rollup_usage_events_before, before inserting, look up an existing rollup row for the bucket key (using IS NULL comparisons for the nullable dimensions) and, if found, increment event_count/total_duration_ms/total_result_count on that row instead of adding a new one (mirroring SQLAlchemyUsageEventRollupRepository.save). Equivalently, route the merge through the rollup repo's upsert logic. Add a regression test that runs retention twice over events sharing a NULL-dimension bucket and asserts a single merged rollup row.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding db-layer-1
title: Usage-event retention silently creates duplicate rollup buckets, double-counting analytics (relates to telemetry retention lab-tracker-uk45.10 — the rollup must be idempotent)

description:
RepositoryDecisionContextReader.search() calls query_questions()/query_notes() with a search pattern and a limit but does NOT pass recent_first. The underlying query (sqlalchemy_repository_parts/core.py:526-527 and notes.py:158-159) therefore defaults to ORDER BY created_at ASC, question_id ASC. So when a project has more matching questions/notes than `limit` (default 20, easy for a common term in a real lab), the 'search_match' slice returns the OLDEST matches and silently discards the most recent ones. This directly undermines the tool's purpose (surfacing the most relevant/current reasoning before a research decision) and the documented retrieval_policy 'explicit_links_then_search_then_recency'. The recency payloads correctly use recent_first=True, so the search slice is the odd one out and the two slices fight each other for the limited budget.

Fix: Pass recent_first=True (or add an updated_first ordering) to the query_questions/query_notes calls inside search() so the search slice surfaces the newest matches, consistent with the recency payloads. Alternatively expose ordering on the reader.search signature and have build_decision_context request recency ordering.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding decision-context-1
title: Search seam returns OLDEST matches first and drops newer ones (created_at ASC, no recent_first)

description:
truncation() is computed only over the recency payloads (questions_payload, notes_payload, ...). The search_payload built by reader.search() reports meta.questions_count/notes_count as the number of RETURNED items (decision_context_query.py:201), not the total number of matches, and it is not included in the truncation list at all. Combined with the oldest-first ordering above, when a project has more matching questions/notes than `limit`, the response silently omits matches AND reports truncation.was_truncated=False for the search dimension. An assistant consuming this payload has no way to know relevant evidence was dropped, which is dangerous for a system whose explicit job is to prevent decisions made on incomplete context.

Fix: Have reader.search() return the true total match counts (query_questions/query_notes already return total) in meta, and include the search payload in the truncation() sections so was_truncated reflects dropped search matches. At minimum, surface a 'search' truncation section keyed off returned vs. total matches.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding decision-context-2
title: Search-slice truncation is invisible: no was_truncated signal when matches exceed limit

description:
Every write tool (lab_tracker_create_project/question/note/dataset/analysis/claim/claim_edge/visualization/goal, update_goal, link_node_to_goal, upload_visualization_file, refactor_question, record_evidence_bundle) wraps the client call in only `try: ... finally: client.close()`. No except clause catches LabTrackerAPIError/LabTrackerAPIValidationError/LabTrackerAPIAuthError/LabTrackerAPIUnavailableError/httpx.HTTPError. By contrast, read tools route every call through _read_tool (src/lab_tracker/mcp_tools/read.py:40-53), which converts failures into the structured envelope produced by lab_tracker_unavailable / lab_tracker_api_error (error.code, status_code, issues, and a next_action hint the agent is instructed to follow). When a write fails, FastMCP catches the exception and re-raises ToolError (.venv mcp/server/fastmcp/tools/base.py:116-117), which the low-level server turns into a CallToolResult with isError=True and the bare string 'Error executing tool lab_tracker_create_claim: Lab Tracker request POST /claims failed: ...' (mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:583-584). Consequence: on a write the agent loses error.code, the 422 `issues` list (field-level validation detail the client already parses in _append_issue_text), the auth-vs-unavailable distinction, and the next_action guidance — exactly the machine-actionable contract the read path is built around. For irreplaceable research data this makes write failures hard for the agent to recover from correctly (e.g. it cannot reliably tell 'fix your input' from 'service is down, stop retrying').

Fix: Introduce a shared _write_tool helper mirroring _read_tool: catch (LabTrackerAPIUnavailableError, httpx.HTTPError) -> lab_tracker_unavailable(tool_name, detail=...), and LabTrackerAPIError -> lab_tracker_api_error(tool_name, exc), wrapping the structured result with with_next_action, in a try/finally that closes the client. Route all WRITE_TOOLS through it so read and write surfaces return the same structured error envelope. Add tests asserting a failing write tool returns error.code/issues/next_action rather than raising.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding mcp-1
title: Write MCP tools have no error handling, so failures return a raw, unstructured error blob instead of the structured envelope read tools provide

description:
Fix: Add a migration test that, at rev 0022, inserts two goal_links rows sharing (goal_id, entity_type, entity_id, relation) both with slot=NULL, then runs `command.upgrade(config, 'head')` and asserts it succeeds and that exactly one of the duplicate rows survives (the oldest by created_at/link_id, matching the ROW_NUMBER ORDER BY).

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding migrations-2
title: No test exercises the goal-link dedupe DELETE path, masking the 0023/0041 ordering regression

description:
In `_ara_logic_graph`, the goal node is added via `_goal_node(...)` (line 1317), which calls `_apply_origin_provenance` (provenance.py:1481). For a Goal with `origin == USER_REVISED` and a `change_set_id`, that helper emits `prov:wasRevisionOf` pointing at a `.../goals/<id>/versions/before/<change_set_id>` IRI and a `changeSet`/`prov:wasGeneratedBy` reference to the draft-activity IRI. Unlike every other entity type in this module (claims, datasets, analyses, questions, notes, visualizations — each of which pairs `_apply_origin_provenance` with a `_merge_graph_nodes(merged, _origin_provenance_nodes(...))` call), the goal branch never calls `_origin_provenance_nodes(base_url, records.goal)`. Goal also carries `origin`, `change_set_id`, `origin_provider`, `origin_model`, `origin_prompt_version` (models.py:824-828). Consequence: for any AI-suggested or AI-revised goal, the exported Ara logic layer contains dangling references — the draft `prov:Activity`, the `prov:SoftwareAgent` (with aiProvider/aiModel/aiPromptVersion), and the pre-revision 'before' `prov:Entity` are missing, so the JSON-LD graph is not self-consistent and the AI-origin attribution for the goal is silently lost. test_provenance.py:269 explicitly asserts this self-consistency invariant for visualizations but no equivalent test exists for goals.

Fix: After adding the goal node in `_ara_logic_graph`, mirror the other entity branches: `_merge_graph_nodes(merged, _origin_provenance_nodes(base_url, records.goal))`. Add a regression test that builds an Ara artifact for an AI_SUGGESTED/USER_REVISED goal and asserts the draft activity, software agent, and (for USER_REVISED) the before-revision node are all present in the logic-layer @graph.

Source: deep review 2026-06-19 finding provenance-1
title: Goal origin/revision edges in Ara logic layer reference nodes that are never materialized (dangling JSON-LD)

acceptance_criteria: A PI can evaluate the product without a build (hosted demo or screenshots); a lab member who is "the techy one" can stand up a shared instance with roughly one command and create the first admin + invite members from a UI; a bench scientist can reach phone capture and write notes after being given a link + login.
description:
Lab Tracker's stated audience is wet-lab bench scientists and PIs (README.md:17-19), but every documented path to a running app is a developer/terminal workflow. An audit (2026-06-15) found there is no hosted URL, no GUI installer, and no download-and-run path: the first Quickstart instruction is `uv venv` (README.md:24), the GitHub repo has an empty homepageUrl and zero releases, and the realistic shared-lab path is 15+ terminal commands across up to 7 tools (uv/Python, Node/npm, Docker, Postgres, Dolt, Beads).

Key finding: the wall is SETUP/DEPLOYMENT, not day-to-day clicking. Once someone technical stands up a server, a non-technical scientist CAN reach the browser/phone PWA and log in — but no one in a typical wet lab can do that setup unaided, and several end-user dead-ends remain (read-only self-registration, no onboarding, admin bootstrap only via raw HTTP POST).

This epic groups the docs, launcher, deployment, and in-app onboarding work that lowers the barrier so a bench scientist/PI can evaluate and use Lab Tracker without engineering support. Children are tagged [quick-win] / [medium] / [larger] by effort in their titles.
title: Non-technical onboarding: make Lab Tracker usable by bench scientists & PIs without a terminal

description:
The PI wants Lab Tracker to represent GOALS (aspirational research outputs: papers, grants, talks) and let existing graph nodes (questions, claims, datasets, analyses, visualizations) be tagged 'in relation to' a goal output (e.g. 'this figure is a candidate for Figure 3 of paper X', 'this claim addresses Aim 2 of grant Y'). The relation is often tentative ('possible'), and goal types are heterogeneous, so the representation must be flexible.

Chosen design (from a multi-approach design review): a first-class project-scoped 'goals' table with a validated JSON 'attributes' blob, plus a polymorphic 'goal_links' tag table modeled on NoteTargetModel and carrying a relation + link_status pair like dataset_question_links. Flexibility comes from a per-goal-type Pydantic registry over the JSON attributes (extra='forbid' per type + an 'other' escape hatch), NOT per-type subtables. Goals are a new EntityType node in the graph; creating a goal is direct CRUD, while tagging a node to a goal rides the human-gated GraphChangeSet spine.

v1 decisions: goal types = paper, grant, talk (+ 'other' escape hatch; thesis_chapter/patent are trivial later additions). goal_links uses a synthetic link_id PK so a node can hold multiple relations/slots per goal.

Build-vs-buy guardrail: stays a thin semantic layer on the PROV-O reasoning spine (pointers + edges + light metadata). It must NOT grow into a manuscript editor / reference manager / grants-management or slot-coverage board; that is the line recorded in docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md.
design: Base approach: json-attrs-entity. Tables: goals (goal_id PK, project_id CASCADE FK, goal_type, title, summary Text, status, target_date Date, external_ref String(1000), attributes sa.JSON, created_by, created_at/updated_at; index on project_id,created_at) and goal_links (link_id String(36) PK, goal_id CASCADE FK, entity_type String(30), entity_id String(36), relation String(40), link_status String(20) default candidate, slot String(120) nullable, created_by, created_at; UNIQUE(goal_id,entity_type,entity_id,relation,slot); index ix_goal_links_entity_lookup on entity_type,entity_id,goal_id mirroring ix_note_targets_entity_lookup; index on goal_id,link_status). Enums: GoalType(paper,grant,talk,other), GoalStatus(planned,in_progress,submitted,accepted,abandoned), GoalRelation(contributes_to,addresses,candidate_figure,supporting_evidence,background,methods), GoalLinkStatus(candidate,committed,dropped). EntityType gains GOAL. JSON columns are plain sa.JSON() per repo convention (no JSONB in this codebase). Single alembic head confirmed = 0021_claim_questions (down_revision for new migration 0022).
notes: Source: design workflow synthesis (5 approaches, 4 adversarial lens-judges). Verified against live code: single alembic head 0021_claim_questions; _CREATE_SCHEMAS/_UPDATE_SCHEMAS/_SEMANTIC_ALLOWED_TARGETS dispatch maps in services/graph_draft_validation.py; LINK_NOTE_TO_* family modeled as (UPDATE, NOTE) so there is no generic link primitive (a goal UPDATE applier branch is required); JSON columns use sa.JSON() not JSONB.
title: Goals/outputs: flexible goal entity + node-tagging on the provenance spine

description: Deep review 2026-06-12 (docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md) found that referential integrity relies on DB cascades that never fire on the default SQLite runtime (no PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON) and 500 on Postgres, while service delete paths (question/dataset/analysis) perform no referential checks, silently corrupting committed provenance records. This epic tracks FK enforcement, delete guards, and schema-drift cleanup.

description: src/lab_tracker/db.py get_engine never sets PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, so every ondelete CASCADE/SET NULL rule in db_models.py is a no-op on the default SQLite backend (verified orphans), and there is no WAL or busy timeout for the multi-client runtime (db.py:16 and :24). Add a connect-event listener for sqlite URLs (foreign_keys=ON, journal_mode=WAL, busy_timeout) plus a regression test asserting cascades fire. From deep review 2026-06-12; details in docs/runs/deep-review-2026-06-12.md.
title: Enable SQLite FK enforcement plus WAL and busy_timeout

This is the cross-cutting enabler that makes pointer-not-reimplementation real and positions Lab Tracker as the integration layer rather than a competitor to any single tool.

acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduled agent runs at the user-set cadence, idempotently, with configurable window
- Cadence is a user setting; changing it reschedules the agent
- Batch context builder collects all notes since last successful run + relevant graph slice
- Draft generator produces a structured proposal set covering the batch
- A single report/review surface summarizes all proposed changes in the batch (tabs per change optional), with per-operation accept/reject
- Approved operations commit through the existing graph mutation path
- Rejected/edited operations are recorded for future model feedback
- Notification surfaces when a new batch is ready for review
description:
Replace per-note draft generation with a scheduled batch at a cadence the user sets. Drafting on every upload thrashes context and wastes model calls on incomplete information; a batch cadence lets the model see accumulated notes together, dedupe, propose coherent multi-note merges, and produce a single review queue.

Goal: at the user-set cadence (daily is a sensible default, not a requirement), a scheduled agent wakes up, collects all notes that landed since the last run, builds a graph-aware context packet covering them, tries to figure out proposed graph operations (new nodes, edges, claim updates), and stores the result as a pending batch in the existing graph-draft review UI. The human reviews per batch instead of per note.

Pairs with the 'PWA capture-first phone workflow' epic: capture cheaply through the day, review proposals in one sitting.
design:
Batch is the unit of review, not the individual note. Cadence is a user-facing setting: setting or changing it (re)schedules an agent that wakes up at that cadence, reads the accumulated inputs, and tries to figure out the changes. Runner is idempotent (re-runnable on the same window without duplicates). Context builder pulls unprocessed notes + the relevant graph slice (projects/questions touched). Draft generator can propose merges across multiple notes (e.g. three photos from the same gel become one observation). Review UI extends the existing graph-draft card pattern to a batch container.

Report/review surface decisions (2026-06-10): review is expected to happen at a computer, so do NOT constrain report layout for phones (fine if it happens to render there, but never a design constraint). One report summarizes all proposed changes in a batch; tabs per proposed change (or per change category) are an acceptable way to organize it.
title: Epic: Scheduled AI graph-draft batch (user-set cadence)

acceptance_criteria: An agent can call one tool and get a short, ranked list of the highest-signal open questions on active goals (with rationale), or an informative empty result; the ranking is documented and tested.
description:
The one genuine FEATURE gap vs Beads. Beads' killer move is `ready`: a short list of unblocked, actionable items that gives an agent an obvious entry action. lab-tracker's `readiness` is infra/DB health (src/lab_tracker/mcp_tools/read.py:19-23), not a work queue, and there is no work-queue tool at all (grep for next_step/ready_question/suggest_next in src/ is empty).

Build a graph-native analog, e.g. `lab_tracker_next_questions` / `open_threads`: active goals -> their active/staged questions not yet answered or linked to a claim -> ranked. This is NOT a 1:1 port: Beads ranks over a task dependency DAG; lab-tracker has goals + questions + notes, so the RANKING SIGNAL is the hard design problem (recency? linked-note count? on the critical path to a goal? question staged vs active?). Medium effort, not trivial.

Value caveat to record on the issue: the payoff is GATED on graph hygiene — if a lab doesn't maintain goals/questions, the tool returns nothing useful. Worth building, but expectations should be set accordingly, and the empty result should itself be informative ("no active goals with open questions — consider creating/activating a goal").
design: Define the candidate set (active goals -> active/staged unanswered questions) and a defensible ranking heuristic; expose as a read-only tool returning a short ranked list with the goal each question advances and why it surfaced. Reuse the decision-context query layer (decision_context_query.py) where possible.
title: [feature] Graph-native "ready work" tool: surface open questions on active goals as the obvious next move

description: Findings from the 2026-07-15 ArjanCodes-style deep review of the Python consumer, MCP client, watch/repo/HPC automation, and capture helpers. acceptance_criteria: Corrupt-first/valid-second drains the valid record and quarantines/reports the corrupt one; terminal-first with limit=1 reaches the first pending record; watch/repo/HPC share the same tested semantics; concurrent writers cannot collide or truncate records; scheduled runs expose durable failure status even when console output is suppressed.
description:
watch.py, repo.py, and hpc.py each decode event files before the per-record recovery block and slice the oldest files before filtering terminal states. One malformed/unsupported record aborts every later record; with a limit, an already-synced oldest record can starve pending work forever. Scheduled --fail-silent runs can hide the stall, and the three copies already differ in temporary-file safety.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Put an already-synced event a.json before pending b.json and drain with limit=1; repeat and observe b.json is never processed.
2. Separately put malformed a.json before valid b.json.
3. Drain through watch, repo, or HPC sync and observe the decode exception aborts the batch before b.json.
design: Extract one typed Outbox component with an injected event codec and processor. Decode/validate/process inside a per-record boundary, quarantine unreadable events with an observable error, select actionable events before applying limit, and use unique atomic writes plus explicit concurrency control.
title: Unify outbox draining so bad or terminal records cannot starve pending work

acceptance_criteria: A failed capture against endpoint A does not skip a healthy explicit client/endpoint B; a breaker recovers after its cooldown/half-open probe; concurrent captures do not race on shared timeout state; using the exported proxy in supported patterns cannot leave a closed cached client; environment/profile changes are observed after recreation; regression tests cover each lifecycle.
description:
Figure capture uses a permanent process-global circuit flag: one transient endpoint failure skips all later captures, including calls with a healthy explicit client. Separately, the exported lazy singleton can be used as a context manager that closes its cached httpx client without clearing the cache, leaving subsequent module-level helpers attached to a closed client.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Cause one savefig call to fail with a connection error.
2. Call savefig with a healthy explicit client and observe it is skipped because the process-global circuit is open.
3. Separately use the exported lazy client in a with block, exit it, then call a module-level helper and observe reuse of the closed httpx client.
design: Give circuit-breaker state explicit per-client/per-endpoint ownership with cooldown, half-open retry, observability, and reset. Remove context-manager ownership from the global proxy or make each context own a fresh client and clear it deterministically. Request timeouts must not mutate a shared client's private timeout state.
title: Remove process-global client lifecycle traps from capture helpers

acceptance_criteria: Python helper, CLI, MCP guidance, and server defaults agree that new agent/consumer questions and notes are staged; activate/commit requires an explicit named operation; tests prove omission cannot activate/commit; generated skill/reference documentation reflects the behavior.
description:
LabTracker.upsert_question defaults to ACTIVE while upsert_note and the lt note command default to COMMITTED, contradicting canonical server defaults and generated guidance that agents may stage evidence but must not accept or commit it. A caller can cross the human gate by omitting a status argument.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call LabTracker.upsert_question without status and inspect the created question; it is active.
2. Call LabTracker.upsert_note or lt note without status and inspect the created note; it is committed.
3. Compare with the server create defaults, which stage both records.
design: Omit status by default and inherit the server's canonical staged state. Expose activation/commit as separately named commands requiring explicit caller intent. Keep backwards compatibility only through deliberate opt-in arguments with migration notes.
title: Default consumer writes to staged and make human transitions explicit

acceptance_criteria: Ambiguous retries and concurrent identical calls produce one canonical entity or a deterministic conflict; changed canonical fields are updated or rejected explicitly rather than ignored; return values distinguish created/reused/updated; pagination cannot hide a match; compatibility and concurrency tests pass.
description: upsert_project and upsert_question are client-side list-then-create operations. Concurrent callers can create duplicates, and an existing natural-key match is returned while changed description, status, type, hypothesis, or parents are silently ignored. The current name promises update semantics the implementation does not provide.
design: Choose an explicit contract: rename to get_or_create with a created/reused outcome and conflict detection, or implement a server-side atomic upsert/idempotency command. Compare canonical supplied fields; never silently discard conflicting intent. Coordinate with MCP natural-key disclosure without assuming database uniqueness for every domain entity.
title: Make upsert helpers atomic and honest about conflicting input

design: Extract a neutral wire/transport layer for auth, request execution, pagination, envelopes, and typed errors while retaining separate use-case façades. description: NoteModel/NoteTargetModel plus project organization overlap heavily with Electronic Lab Notebooks (eLabFTW, Benchling, RSpace, LabArchives) - the biggest mindshare overlap but the worst conceptual fit, since ELNs are document-centric while Lab Tracker is graph-centric. Decide the boundary: integrate with / link out to an ELN, or deliberately avoid ELN scope creep - but do NOT become an ELN.
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: where a lab already uses an ELN, a note can reference an ELN entry (URI + hash) and Lab Tracker keeps the edges the ELN does not model - which question/claim/dataset the note attaches to (NoteTargetModel). Keep the human-gated note-to-graph draft->commit flow (GraphChangeSet/GraphChangeOperation) in-house as a differentiator. Resist adding rich-document/editor features that pull toward becoming an ELN.

acceptance_criteria: restore refuses when a ProcessLock on <db>.lock is held (test simulates a live idle server, no active txn); existing active-BEGIN-EXCLUSIVE refusal still passes; _copy_sqlite_database round-trips a path containing '?'; _sqlite_ro_uri emits a valid absolute file:// URI for a Windows drive-letter path and encodes special chars; full pytest + ruff green; lifespan lock does not disturb the existing TestClient integration suite.
description:
Deep review of the merged backup/restore code (src/lab_tracker/backup.py, PR range 140feda..f64ecc8) found a blocking data-integrity defect plus two related backup defects.

BLOCKING: restore_sqlite_backup()'s _assert_database_not_locked() probes with BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, but SQLite locks are transaction-scoped, not connection-scoped. The server runs WAL mode with a SQLAlchemy pool whose connections sit idle between requests; an idle connection does NOT block BEGIN EXCLUSIVE. So a --force restore against a *running* server passes the guard, deletes the live -wal/-shm sidecars, and os.replace()s the DB file under the live process -> torn DB / corruption. The only test holds an ACTIVE BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, so it never exercises the realistic idle-pool state.

RELATED 1: _copy_sqlite_database builds the read-only source URI as f'file:{as_posix()}?mode=ro'. On Windows as_posix() yields C:/... producing a RELATIVE 'file:C:/...' URI (must be file:///C:/...). Paths containing ? or # are also unescaped, silently producing an EMPTY backup that passes integrity_check. POSIX CI never catches it.

RELATED 2: _assert_sqlite_integrity opens the restore source read-WRITE (no mode=ro), touching mtime and potentially spawning sidecars; the backup copy path already uses mode=ro.
design: Cooperative OS advisory lock. New module process_lock.py provides a cross-platform best-effort exclusive ProcessLock (fcntl.flock on POSIX, msvcrt.locking on Windows) on a <db>.lock sidecar; the OS releases it on process exit so a crash leaves no stale lock. The running server acquires it for its lifetime in make_lifespan() (best-effort, sqlite-only, never crashes startup; Postgres/:memory: get no lock). The offline restore process acquires the same lock non-blocking around the destructive section and refuses if it cannot (server is live). BEGIN EXCLUSIVE retained as a secondary active-transaction check. URI fixes: a single _sqlite_ro_uri() helper uses Path.as_uri() (emits file:///C:/... and percent-encodes ?/#) + '?mode=ro', used by both _copy_sqlite_database and _assert_sqlite_integrity (now read-only).
title: Harden SQLite backup/restore: cooperative live-server lock + cross-platform read-only URI

acceptance_criteria: Replacement LPAT is active before old expiry, hosted MCP protocol/read checks pass, unauthenticated calls remain denied, old token is revoked after verification, and no credential appears in logs.

design: Use the existing operator identity and a bounded-lifetime VIEWER read-only token. Store only the token in the private runtime env; no research graph records or account memberships need changing.
title: Rotate hosted MCP read-only LPAT before 2026-12-30

description: Clean PR 1 validation on macOS reproduces failures in tests/test_repo_git_state.py and tests/test_worktree_tree.py on unchanged code. The health deadline tests and escaped-descendant test also fail on this Python 3.13 macOS runtime; classify separately before altering runtime behavior.
design: Use explicit helper executable paths or a portable controlled PATH in timeout fixtures. Keep the timeout assertions and production behavior unchanged. Confirm timer/descendant failures against the supported Linux/Python 3.11 CI runtime before assigning a cause.

description: Audit of src/lab_tracker/frontend_src/features/graph-drafts.jsx (the AI-revise composer, separate surface from mobile capture) found three confirmed recording defects: (1) record-reentrancy-stream-leak (medium): startRecording (536-579) is async and only sets isRecording=true AFTER getUserMedia resolves (573); a second click during the permission/await window re-enters and overwrites audioStreamRef/mediaRecorderRef without stopping the first stream -> leaked live mic MediaStream + orphaned MediaRecorder. Fix: set an in-flight flag before awaiting and bail if refs already populated. (2) stop-button-gated-by-caneditdraft (medium): the single toggle button is disabled={!canEditDraft} (918); if an operation action flips changeSet.status mid-recording, Stop becomes unreachable and the mic stays live until unmount. Fix: disabled={isRecording ? false : !canEditDraft} or a useEffect that stops recording when canEditDraft goes false. (3) dictate-not-gated-by-canrecordaudio (low): button not gated by canRecordAudio(), so on unsupported browsers it looks enabled and only fails on click. Fix: const recordingSupported=canRecordAudio(); disabled={!canEditDraft || !recordingSupported}. Found by capture-ui-audit workflow; all three adversarially verified high-confidence.
title: AI-revise 'Dictate feedback' recorder: re-entrancy stream leak + unstoppable mid-recording + no capability gate

description: Backend records current state but rarely WHEN or WHY state changed, so PI review questions about latency, queue depth, time-in-status, decision loops, and zombie projects are unanswerable despite visible counts. This epic captures human-gated transition moments (reviews, decisions, QC verdicts, blocked reasons, status changes) plus epistemic-trust tags, then derives metrics from the existing portfolio aggregation (routes/portfolio.py) and PROV-O traversal. Commodity domains (protocols, rigs, QC reports, colony, inventory) stay pointer-plus-edge or are declined per docs/build-vs-buy-boundaries.md. Sourced from the 2026-06-16 gap analysis against the lab systems-design doc.
design: Five phases by leverage-per-effort. Phase 0 = pure derivation (no migration). Phases 1-3 = the moat capture. Phase 4 = gated on demonstrated lab demand. DECLINE LIST (do NOT build): animal/colony manager, reagent inventory, equipment/calibration registry, full protocol/ELN entity, generic blocker/task/PM system, HR/career/conflict-case fields, standing RBAC authority matrix, QC computation/dashboards, automated kill-criteria evaluation, configurable workflow stages. Where the doc wants visibility into these, capture only the reason/pointer, never the system of record.
title: PI lab-health visibility: capture state-transition data for review

acceptance_criteria: A fresh MCP-connected session shows a lab-tracker entry in the client's "MCP Server Instructions" with a crisp, trigger-enumerated consult directive; the string is sourced from (not duplicated against) the existing policy constant.
description:
The single biggest, cheapest salience lever. `server = FastMCP(SERVER_NAME)` (src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py:64) passes no `instructions=`, so lab-tracker injects nothing into the agent system prompt — it was absent from this session's "MCP Server Instructions" block while Beads/scite/consensus appeared. FastMCP supports an `instructions=` kwarg that MCP clients (e.g. Claude Code) surface in-context.

The content already exists: reuse AGENT_CONSULTATION_POLICY (src/lab_tracker/decision_context_constants.py:16) — distilled to a few sentences — and point at the lab-tracker://quickstart resource. CRITICAL design note: unlike Beads (whose trigger "we track work" fires every session), lab-tracker's trigger ("research-facing decision") is occasional and fuzzy, so the instructions MUST enumerate the trigger crisply (what to plot, which analysis/control, figures, summaries, manuscript/grant text) rather than say a vague "consult before research," or agents won't know when it fires.

Example:
  server = FastMCP(SERVER_NAME, instructions=(
    "This lab uses Lab Tracker as the system of record for research reasoning. "
    "BEFORE research-facing decisions (what to plot, which analysis/control, figures, "
    "summaries, manuscript/grant/abstract text) call `lab_tracker_get_decision_context`. "
    "Read `lab-tracker://quickstart` for setup. Do not mutate records unless asked."))
design: Keep instructions as a single source of truth shared with AGENT_CONSULTATION_POLICY/AGENTS.md so the three copies don't drift; consider deriving the short instructions string from the policy constant. Verify the string actually appears in a Claude Code session's MCP Server Instructions block after the change.
title: [activation] Set FastMCP `instructions=` to wire the existing consultation policy into agents' system prompt

acceptance_criteria: Docs and detection make the rclone-portable vs local_fs-single-host distinction explicit and state the 'no setup on hosts you cannot control' rule; a shared OneDrive store resolves on at least two heterogeneous hosts (laptop + one other) via the recommended form.
description: Setup is multi-host: a lab has her laptop, instrument/experiment PCs, and a shared core-facility PC — not one server. But DataStoreModel has a SINGLE root + credential_ref per store (db_models.py:1064-1069), so a shared logical store (e.g. lab-onedrive) has ONE root. Consequence: rclone kinds are host-portable (credential_ref = an rclone remote NAME each host maps in its own rclone.conf; root = in-remote path), but a local_fs store's root is an absolute host path that only matches the machine that registered it — a synced-folder store is effectively single-host. check_store_health and the resolvers are explicitly 'from this host' (artifact_resolution.py), so resolution already degrades cleanly per host, but there is no way to bind one shared store to different local access on different machines. Decide/implement: (a) steer multi-host labs to the rclone form as the portable default (detection preference + docs; reserve local_fs for a single machine) with NO schema change, and/or (b) add a per-host store-binding (host -> local root/credential override) so a synced folder can bind differently per machine. Also make explicit: hosts that can't be set up (shared core PC) need NO local Lab Tracker setup — they just upload to the store, and another host resolves + hashes the file (this is the G7 softening).
title: Per-host binding for shared data stores (rclone remote = portable fleet access vs host-pinned local_fs root)

acceptance_criteria: An agent in a fresh session is oriented toward Lab Tracker at message one (server instructions present), knows to call get_decision_context before research-facing decisions, has an obvious "what should I advance" entry action, and degrades gracefully (clear "Lab Tracker unavailable, proceeding without graph context") when the API is down rather than treating the failure as its own.
description:
Audience: AI coding/research agents (NOT bench scientists — kept separate from the onboarding epic lab-tracker-chv8).

A 2026-06-16 comparison with the Beads MCP found that lab-tracker already has the hard part Beads lacks — a provenance/knowledge graph with `lab_tracker_get_decision_context` — and the salience CONTENT is already written: MCP resources `lab-tracker://quickstart`, `lab-tracker://surface`, `lab-tracker://agent-consultation-policy` (src/lab_tracker/mcp_tools/resources.py:43-58), the AGENT_CONSULTATION_POLICY (src/lab_tracker/decision_context_constants.py:16), and a consult block in AGENTS.md:28-43.

What is missing is ACTIVATION at the two injection points that actually fire, plus the reliability that makes activation safe:
1. The MCP server is built as `FastMCP(SERVER_NAME)` with NO `instructions=` argument (src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py:64) — so lab-tracker contributes nothing to the agent's system prompt (it was absent from this session's "MCP Server Instructions" block while Beads/scite/consensus were present). This is the single biggest, cheapest lever.
2. There is no lab-tracker SessionStart/conditional hook or managed CLAUDE.md block; the only session hook runs `bd prime` (Beads).
3. Reliability tax: lab-tracker is HTTP-backed and is 502-ing. Salience without reliability is NEGATIVE — items that raise the call rate against a failing endpoint teach agents to abandon the tool. Hardening + a fail-soft error contract is a co-prerequisite, not a footnote.

Design principle: Beads' model does not port 1:1. Beads is frequent + local + behavioral-trigger; lab-tracker is occasional + networked + semantic-trigger. Adaptations must be conditional, fail-soft, and trigger-defined — not an unconditional networked prime, and not a routing god-tool.

Explicitly NOT in scope: Dolt/SQLite/daemon sync, native-binary install, a single routing god-tool.
title: MCP salience & activation: make AI agents reliably reach for Lab Tracker

description:
Deferred from the daily-review redesign ('The Morning Read') design session. The redesign escalates always-on bench PHOTOGRAPHY (hero photos surface whatever was incidentally in frame — people, whiteboards with unpublished ideas, IACUC/PHI-relevant subjects), VOICE feedback (ambient lab audio sent to a third-party transcription provider), optional TTS read-aloud (drafted prose sent to a TTS provider — a new third-party egress), and Phase-3 push notifications whose content is lockscreen-visible unpublished science. None of the daily-review design lenses addressed privacy/governance; the product owner has explicitly deferred it for now but wants to revisit before any of these multimodal/push surfaces ship.

This is a PREREQUISITE for: featuring user photos as hero/illustration in the daily review, voice-as-feedback input, TTS output, and push notifications. It is NOT blocking the Phase-1 reading-column reskin or text-based NL feedback.

Decide and document the defaults: what leaves the building (provider egress for voice/TTS/image), what is visible to teammates vs. on a lockscreen, voice-off-by-default?, a 'don't feature this photo' control, and per-capture sensitivity tagging. Tie to retained-v1-surface philosophy and the existing shared-project membership model.

acceptance_criteria: All three child slices designed (design docs); at least the data-model slice (decision/dead_end/pivot capture) shipped; retained-v1 human gate preserved (nothing auto-commits); single Alembic head maintained; PROV-O export extended to emit the new exploration nodes and edges.
description:
Lab Tracker has independently converged on the epistemic backbone of the Agent-Native Research Artifact (ARA) protocol (arXiv:2604.24658v3, "The Last Human-Written Paper"): the same provenance taxonomy (EntityOrigin = user/ai_suggested/ai_executed/user_revised, models.py:252), the claim<->analysis<->dataset<->question PROV-O binding spine (provenance.py), typed claim relations (ClaimEdge: extends/contradicts/refutes/depends_on/supersedes, models.py:190), staged->committed crystallization, and human-gated AI proposals (GraphChangeSet). That convergence validates the design.

But Lab Tracker preserves only the convergent RESULT graph (question -> dataset -> analysis -> claim) and discards the divergent EXPLORATION graph that the paper's data identifies as the single highest-value signal. ARA's evaluation finds negative knowledge (dead ends, rejected hypotheses) produces the largest accuracy gain in the whole study (their Claim C06); on RE-Bench, failed runs are 90.2% of cost with a median 113x failed-to-success token ratio. Today Lab Tracker's only representation of that knowledge is the free-text terminal_reason on abandoned/superseded entities (migration 0034) and QuestionRefactor.reason, and it harvests staged human artifacts (notes/photos/voice) rather than the researcher-agent conversation that the paper argues is the free byproduct worth capturing.

This epic adds the missing exploration-trajectory layer, scoped to Lab Tracker's retained-v1 human-gated and build-vs-buy boundaries, in three slices:
1. First-class decision/dead_end/pivot capture (beyond free-text terminal_reason).
2. Falsification criteria + verification plan on Claims.
3. A session-end retrospective that distills the agent conversation into the existing daily-review queue.

OUT OF SCOPE (CS-reproduction-specific and/or conflicting with build-vs-buy): ARA's /src kernel-code layer, the ARA Compiler (legacy-PDF ingest), and Seal Certificates. Code stays referenced by hash/URI, never reimplemented.

Reference: github.com/AmberLJC/Agent-Native-Research-Artifact (Live Research Manager skill is open-source).
design:
Framing: ARA and Lab Tracker solve sibling problems from opposite ends (ARA = preserve a branching CS/ML research trajectory as an agent-executable package; Lab Tracker = preserve lab reasoning as a queryable PROV-O graph). The convergence on EntityOrigin, the binding spine, and human-gated proposals is strong external validation of Lab Tracker's core thesis (knowledge over narrative).

Where Lab Tracker is strongest is exactly ARA's Table 5 weakest column for prior tools: cross-layer bindings (the PROV-O spine is the whole reason Lab Tracker exists). The gap is the exploration-trajectory column, which Lab Tracker scores absent on.

Risk the paper itself flags (its extension experiments): a recorded "prior-run playbook" can CONSTRAIN a more capable agent into the prior box. Therefore exploration/dead-end capture must INFORM future work, not hard-gate it.

Boundary check (see memory build-vs-buy-boundary-principle-for-lab-tracker): "which hypothesis we abandoned and why" is irreducible core that no external tool (ELN, experiment tracker, data versioner) models, so it is correct to BUILD it here rather than offload. Relates to memory meeting-aware-daily-review-design (the daily review = the existing graph-draft batch; slice 3 reuses that path).

Process: follow the repo pattern (deep-think design doc -> phased child backlog -> code), and keep a single Alembic head throughout. Extend PROV-O export to emit the new exploration nodes/edges so the lossless-export guarantee still holds.
title: Adopt ARA exploration-trajectory + negative-knowledge capture (arXiv:2604.24658)

acceptance_criteria: A staged/committed dead_end records hypothesis+failure_mode+lesson and links to its source entity; a decision records alternatives-considered; a pivot records trigger+rationale; nodes form a traversable DAG; PROV-O export emits the nodes and edges; human gate preserved (no auto-commit); single Alembic head; tests cover the new model and export.
description:
PROBLEM. Lab Tracker's only representation of process/negative knowledge is the free-text terminal_reason on abandoned/superseded Question/Dataset/Analysis/Claim (added in migration 0034) plus QuestionRefactor.reason. This collapses the structure ARA shows is most valuable. "We abandoned Q (terminal_reason='low SNR')" loses the hypothesis, the failure mode, and the lesson that would stop the next person or agent from re-running the dead end. The current model is a linear supersession chain, not a DAG.

GOAL. Add typed exploration nodes mirroring ARA's exploration_tree.yaml node kinds:
- decision -> { choice, alternatives[], evidence/rationale }
- dead_end -> { hypothesis, failure_mode, lesson }
- pivot    -> { trigger, rationale, invalidates: <prior decision/claim> }
Each node carries EntityOrigin provenance (reuse the existing enum) and links to the entity it concerns (question/dataset/analysis/claim). Edges form a DAG (parent->child plus an also_depends_on style convergence link), so branches and convergence points are traversable -- ARA's "git log for research". Extend PROV-O export to emit the nodes/edges.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (resolve in a design doc first, per repo pattern):
- New entity vs. promoting terminal_reason into a structured ExplorationNode/TerminalEvent table.
- Relationship to QuestionRefactor (already stores reason + snapshots) and ClaimEdge (already typed relations) -- avoid duplicating, prefer one exploration substrate.
- Polymorphic target (like NoteTarget / GoalLink entity_type+entity_id) vs. dedicated table.
- Single Alembic head; one additive migration.
design:
Highest-value slice per the paper: ARA Claim C06 (negative knowledge = largest accuracy gain) and the RE-Bench cost data (failed runs 90.2% of cost, 113x token ratio) are the empirical case for first-class dead-end capture. Priority P1 for that reason.

This is irreducible core (build-vs-buy memory): no external ELN / experiment tracker / data-versioner models "the hypothesis we abandoned and why we abandoned it," so build it here. Reuse, do not duplicate: QuestionRefactor.reason and ClaimEdge already carry fragments of decision/pivot semantics -- the design should consolidate onto one exploration substrate rather than add a third overlapping mechanism.

Honor the paper's own caveat: dead-end nodes must inform, not hard-gate, future exploration (a capable agent may legitimately revisit a path that failed under weaker tooling). Consider a model-class/tooling-context tag on dead_end nodes so successors can discount stale failures (ARA suggests exactly this).

Keep the retained-v1 human gate: agent-proposed exploration nodes flow through the existing GraphChangeSet review queue (see child slice 3), they do not auto-commit.
title: Exploration Graph: capture decision/dead_end/pivot as first-class nodes

acceptance_criteria: Claim can record falsification_criteria and a verification-plan link (refuting outcome); status vocabulary supports an in-test state; new fields surfaced in PROV-O export and the MCP create_claim/describe_schema tools and publication-readiness checks; single Alembic head; tests.
description:
PROBLEM. ARA claims carry status hypothesis/testing/supported, an explicit falsification_criteria field, and a proof pointer via an experiments.md verification plan into /evidence. Lab Tracker's Claim (models.py:679) has statement, confidence (a bare float), status proposed/supported/rejected, and external_citations (migration 0037) -- but records nothing about what would falsify the claim or how it was/will be tested. A claim flips to "supported" without ever stating its test, which makes it an assertion-with-a-number rather than a falsifiable scientific claim.

GOAL (additive, low-risk):
- Add falsification_criteria (text) to Claim.
- Add a verification-plan link: which experiment/analysis tests this claim and what outcome would refute it. Reuse the existing ClaimAnalysis / ClaimDataset edges as the proof pointer; the missing piece is the falsification statement and the predicted/refuting outcome. This complements DatasetQuestionLink.outcome_status (unknown/supports/refutes/inconclusive), which already exists at the dataset->question level.
- Consider an interim "testing" status between proposed and supported/rejected.

Surface the new fields in PROV-O export, the MCP create_claim / describe_schema tools, and the publication-readiness checks.
design:
Cheapest high-value slice: additive fields, no structural change. Aligns a Lab Tracker Claim with a falsifiable scientific assertion (the ARA claims.md schema).

Consider requiring falsification_criteria before a Claim may reach status=supported -- the publication-readiness machinery already flags unsupported claims (models.py PublicationReadinessUnsupportedClaim), so this extends an existing gate rather than inventing one.

Keep confidence as-is for now; ARA does not mandate intervals. The win here is the falsification statement + the refuting-outcome link, not richer uncertainty quantification (that is a separate, deferrable concern).

Single Alembic head; one additive migration. Update describe_schema so agents discover the new fields.
title: Falsification criteria + verification plan on Claims

acceptance_criteria: A session-end action distills decisions/dead-ends/rationale from the conversation into PROPOSED exploration/claim/note records (origin ai_suggested, and ai_executed for agent-run experiments) inside a GraphChangeSet visible at /app/batches; nothing auto-commits; provenance tags set correctly so AI_EXECUTED finally has a producer; design doc precedes code.
description:
PROBLEM. ARA's central thesis is that the research trajectory is a free byproduct of every researcher-agent session, captured at session boundaries by a Context Harvester -> Event Router -> Maturity Tracker pipeline (shipped as an agent skill). Lab Tracker's daily review distills STAGED HUMAN ARTIFACTS (notes/photos/voice), not the conversation, and the lab-tracker skill restricts agents to read-only consultation + explicit-only writes with no session-boundary hook (docs/retained-v1-surface.md). Tellingly, EntityOrigin.AI_EXECUTED is defined (models.py:252) but never set -- no code path ever produces it. The agent conversation on this very repo IS a research trajectory (decisions, dead ends, rationale) currently thrown away.

GOAL. Add a session-end retrospective -- an extension of the existing lab-tracker / secretary skill plus a thin write path -- that distills decisions, dead ends, and rationale from the agent conversation into PROPOSED exploration nodes (child slice 1) and notes, landing them in the existing GraphChangeSet daily-review queue (/app/batches, POST /batches/run-due) for human accept/reject. Tag harvested records ai_suggested, and ai_executed where the agent actually ran the experiment (finally giving AI_EXECUTED a producer). The closest analog already ships (skills + scheduled run-due); this points it at the conversation instead of only staged captures.

Study the open-source Live Research Manager skill (github.com/AmberLJC/Agent-Native-Research-Artifact) as a reference implementation of the capture pipeline before designing ours.

Depends on child slice 1 (needs the decision/dead_end/pivot vocabulary to land events into).
design:
Reconciling ARA's "silent, zero-overhead, auto-crystallize" capture with Lab Tracker's deliberate human gate: gate only the COMMIT, not the capture. Harvested events become PROPOSALS in the existing GraphChangeSet review queue -- exactly the mechanism graph drafts already use -- so retained-v1's "no autonomous agent writes" holds (these are proposals, not writes). This is additive, not a philosophy change.

Reuses the meeting-aware daily-review path (memory meeting-aware-daily-review-design): the daily review IS the existing retained graph-draft batch; this adds a conversation-derived source alongside staged notes, not a new draft entry point.

Provenance correctness is a concrete deliverable: AI_EXECUTED gets its first real producer (agent-run experiments), AI_SUGGESTED for inferred decisions/hypotheses, USER_REVISED preserved when the human edits a proposal at review time (graph_draft_applier already sets USER_REVISED on UPDATE).

Depends on child slice 1. Design doc first (deep-think), then phased backlog, matching repo convention.
title: Session-end retrospective: harvest the agent conversation into the daily-review queue

description: Add permission-bounded, read-only project overview, cross-entity search, and typed neighborhood traversal over the retained Lab Tracker graph. These focused API and MCP surfaces let remote agents orient, locate anchors, and inspect nearby evidence without materializing the full project graph. Preserve existing graph, search, list, and decision-context behavior.
design: Implement a query-first application service over existing SQL tables and indexes. Authorize the project and traversal anchor before querying. Aggregate overview counts and entry points, union bounded per-entity substring searches with deterministic exact/prefix/substring ranking, and traverse only the current relationship frontier with deterministic BFS caps. Reuse project-graph node labels, relationship tokens, and semantic mappings. Responses remain summary-first; explicit anchor content is capped at 8000 characters. MCP guidance follows overview to search to neighborhood to mandatory decision context for research-facing decisions. No schema migration, UI, FTS, embeddings, path finding, revision cursor, resource template, or OKF generation.

description: Lab Tracker's durable product is the PROV-O / JSON-LD semantic provenance spine threading questions -> notes -> sessions -> datasets -> analyses -> claims -> visualizations (see src/lab_tracker/provenance.py). It is anchored by two node types no external tool provides: Questions (broad-to-atomic inquiry structure) and Claims (epistemic layer linking evidence to conclusions with confidence). Many adjacent responsibilities are either commodity infrastructure or owned by mature tool categories that Lab Tracker risks accidentally half-reimplementing: identity/RBAC, byte/asset storage, data versioning, experiment tracking, note capture (ELNs), transcription, and search. This epic decomposes the boundary decisions: for each adjacent responsibility decide offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house, so effort concentrates on the irreducible semantic core. Already-resolved boundaries: voice transcription is offloaded to an explicit note-scoped action (retained-v1); multimodal note-to-graph extraction is offloaded to the LLM while the human-gated draft->commit diff stays in-house; semantic/vector search is explicitly deferred in retained-v1.
design: Shared principle - pointer-not-reimplementation: for each adjacent responsibility, store a reference (URI + content hash) to the external tool's artifact PLUS the semantic edges the external tool does not model (which question a dataset addresses, which claim an analysis supports). Do not reimplement the external tool's core. The PROV-O export is the integration seam: ingest external artifacts (DVC/DataLad manifests, MLflow runs, ELN entries) as PROV entities and connect them to inquiry and claims. Integrate decisions should strengthen the core by letting it focus on the semantic graph, not shrink it. Danger zone: each integrate decision is a slippery slope toward rebuilding half of MLflow or half of an ELN - resist field-by-field creep past a reference + edges.
title: Build-vs-buy: define Lab Tracker responsibility boundaries vs existing tools

description:
Make phone note capture nearly effortless. The current /app/capture screen requires login, mandatory project selection, and a network round-trip before anything is saved ? too much friction for one-handed bench work.

Goal: a user takes a photo with their phone's normal Camera app, hits Share, picks Lab Tracker, and the note is staged. No browser open, no login each time, no fields required beyond the captured asset.

This requires turning the existing static-bundle frontend into a Progressive Web App: web app manifest (Add to Home Screen), service worker (offline asset cache + upload retry queue), Web Share Target (OS share-sheet integration), and a device-bound auth path (passkey or long-lived device token) that eliminates the password prompt on phone. The note API also needs a minimal-payload quick-capture endpoint that accepts asset + device-default project and defers all linking to the daily draft review.

Pairs with the 'Daily AI graph-draft batch' epic: capture cheaply now, AI proposes structured graph updates once a day for human review.
design: Phone capture flow target: Camera -> Share Sheet -> Lab Tracker -> staged. <3 taps, works offline. Auth via device-bound passkey/token in IndexedDB, not username/password. Quick-capture endpoint accepts only asset + project; everything else (question/session/dataset links) gets proposed by the daily batch and confirmed in the review card.
